maryMotherOfGod.name: Mary, Mother of God
maryMotherOfGod.bio: On the eighth day after Christmas, the Church celebrates the divine motherhood of the Blessed Virgin Mary. The Council of Ephesus in 431 AD defined Mary as Theotokos -- God-bearer -- against Nestorius, who would have separated the divine and human natures of Christ. To call Mary Mother of God is not to elevate her above God, but to confess that the child she bore in her womb was truly and fully God. She is the first and greatest of the redeemed, the one in whom the Incarnation became flesh.
maryMotherOfGod.prayer: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

saintsBasilTheGreatAndGregoryNazianzenBi.name: Ss. Basil the Great & Gregory Nazianzen
saintsBasilTheGreatAndGregoryNazianzenBi.bio: Basil of Caesarea and Gregory of Nazianzus met as students in Athens and formed one of the great friendships of the early Church. Together with Gregory of Nyssa (Basil's brother), they are called the Cappadocian Fathers. They articulated the doctrine of the Trinity with a precision that has never been surpassed: one God in three Persons, each fully divine, each distinct. Basil founded the first organized monastic communities in the East. Gregory preached sermons of such beauty that they are still read as theological poetry.
saintsBasilTheGreatAndGregoryNazianzenBi.prayer: God our Father, you revealed the mystery of the Trinity through the witness of Basil and Gregory. May their teaching guide us into the depths of your divine life.

theMostHolyNameOfJesus.name: The Holy Name of Jesus
theMostHolyNameOfJesus.bio: The name Jesus -- Yeshua in Hebrew, "God saves" -- was given by the angel before his birth. It is the name at which, Paul writes, every knee shall bow. The devotion to the Holy Name flourished in the medieval period, particularly through the Franciscans and Saint Bernardine of Siena, who promoted the monogram IHS. To speak the name of Jesus in prayer is already to pray -- the Desert Fathers taught that the whole of contemplation could be contained in this one invocation.
theMostHolyNameOfJesus.prayer: Jesus. Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.

tuesdayAfterEpiphany.name: The Epiphany of the Lord
tuesdayAfterEpiphany.bio: The word epiphany means manifestation. On this day the Church celebrates the revelation of Christ to the Gentiles -- represented by the Magi -- and therefore to all the nations. The Magi followed a star. They carried gifts. They found a child. The Church reads into this scene the entire drama of the spiritual life: the long journey, the guidance of obscure signs, the encounter with the one who was sought, and the return home by a different way.
tuesdayAfterEpiphany.prayer: O God, who on this day revealed your only-begotten Son to the nations by the guidance of a star: grant that we, who know you now by faith, may be brought to contemplate the beauty of your majesty.

saintRaymondOfPenyafortPriest.name: St. Raymond of Penyafort
saintRaymondOfPenyafortPriest.bio: Raymond was a Catalan Dominican of the thirteenth century, confessor to Pope Gregory IX, and the man who compiled the Decretals -- the systematic collection of canon law that governed the Church for seven centuries. At the age of sixty-five, having organized the first mendicant missions to the Moors and Jews of Spain, he resigned as Master General of the Dominicans to pursue a life of prayer. He lived to be nearly a hundred. His life is a study in the patience required to build institutions that outlast their founders.
saintRaymondOfPenyafortPriest.prayer: Lord, you gave Raymond the grace to serve both learning and prayer. May we too find in each day's work a form of contemplation.

01-12.name: St. Marguerite Bourgeoys
01-12.bio: Marguerite came to New France in 1653, the first teacher in Montreal. She founded the Congregation of Notre Dame, the first uncloistered religious community in the New World -- women who could move freely through the streets and forests to serve the poor. She refused the comfort of enclosure. Her sisters were called "daughters of the village." She died in 1700, having given fifty years to the children of a colony at the edge of the known world.
01-12.prayer: Saint Marguerite, you went where the need was greatest without waiting for the world to come to you. Give us your courage to move.

saintHilaryOfPoitiersBishopAndDoctor.name: St. Hilary of Poitiers
saintHilaryOfPoitiersBishopAndDoctor.bio: Hilary was a Gallo-Roman bishop of the fourth century who became the great champion of Nicene orthodoxy in the West during the Arian crisis. Exiled to the East by the Emperor Constantius, he used his exile to study Greek theology and returned to the West with a deeper understanding of the Trinity than most Western bishops possessed. He is called the Athanasius of the West. His treatise On the Trinity remains a work of rare precision and depth.
saintHilaryOfPoitiersBishopAndDoctor.prayer: O God, you raised up Hilary to defend the divinity of your Son. Strengthen our faith in the mystery of the Trinity.

saintAnthonyOfEgyptAbbot.name: St. Anthony of Egypt
saintAnthonyOfEgyptAbbot.bio: Anthony was born in Egypt around 251 AD, sold his possessions at twenty years old upon hearing the Gospel read in church, and went into the desert. He is the father of Christian monasticism -- not because he invented solitary prayer, but because his life became the pattern that thousands imitated. Athanasius wrote his biography, and through it Anthony became the most famous Christian in the world by the time he died at 105. The story of his temptations in the desert has never stopped being told.
saintAnthonyOfEgyptAbbot.prayer: O God, who led Anthony into the desert to seek your face: lead us also into that interior solitude where you speak to the heart.

saintsFabianPopeAndSebastianMartyrs.name: St. Fabian
saintsFabianPopeAndSebastianMartyrs.bio: Fabian was elected Pope in 236 AD when, according to tradition, a dove descended on his head during the election -- he had come to Rome merely as a visitor. He organized the Church of Rome into regions served by deacons, established the Liberian Catalogue (the first list of popes), and died a martyr under the Emperor Decius in 250. Saint Cyprian wrote that his death was "worthy of the purity and holiness of his life."
saintsFabianPopeAndSebastianMartyrs.prayer: Lord God, who strengthened Fabian to seal his witness with his blood: grant that we may hold the faith with equal courage.

saintAgnesVirginAndMartyr.name: St. Agnes
saintAgnesVirginAndMartyr.bio: Agnes was twelve or thirteen years old, a Roman girl of noble family, when she was martyred around 304 AD during the persecution of Diocletian. She had consecrated her virginity to Christ, refused marriage to the son of a Roman official, and was executed. She is one of the few women named in the Canon of the Mass. The white lamb -- agnus -- became her symbol. Her youth, her simplicity, and the absoluteness of her fidelity have made her one of the most beloved saints in the calendar.
saintAgnesVirginAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who counted Agnes worthy of the palm of martyrdom in the very flower of her youth: grant that we may follow her in purity of faith and courage of heart.

saintVincentDeaconAndMartyr.name: St. Vincent of Saragossa
saintVincentDeaconAndMartyr.bio: Vincent was a Spanish deacon martyred in Valencia in 304 AD under Diocletian. His bishop, Valerius, was exiled; Vincent was tortured with a rack, iron hooks, a bed of hot coals, and a dungeon spiked with broken pottery. He survived each torment long enough to continue comforting his torturers. Augustine preached two sermons on him. Prudentius wrote a celebrated poem about his passion. His courage became the paradigm of the deacon-martyr in the Western Church.
saintVincentDeaconAndMartyr.prayer: Give us, Lord, through the intercession of Vincent, a love for you strong enough to outlast suffering.

saintFrancisDeSalesBishopAndDoctor.name: St. Francis de Sales
saintFrancisDeSalesBishopAndDoctor.bio: Francis de Sales was bishop of Geneva -- a see largely lost to Calvinism -- and one of the most humanly wise spiritual directors in the tradition. His Introduction to the Devout Life was addressed not to monks but to ordinary people: merchants, mothers, soldiers. He taught that holiness was possible in every state of life, that gentleness was stronger than severity, and that the spiritual life must be adapted to the person, not the person to the spiritual life. His correspondence with Jane de Chantal produced some of the most beautiful letters of spiritual direction ever written.
saintFrancisDeSalesBishopAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who gave Francis de Sales a gentle wisdom for the guidance of souls: teach us, through his intercession, that the love of neighbour is the shortest path to you.

conversionOfSaintPaulApostle.name: The Conversion of St. Paul
conversionOfSaintPaulApostle.bio: Saul of Tarsus was a Pharisee, trained under Gamaliel, a persecutor of the Church by his own description. On the road to Damascus he was thrown to the ground, blinded, and heard a voice: "Saul, Saul, why dost thou persecute me?" The encounter was total and irreversible. He became Paul -- the Apostle to the Gentiles, the author of half the New Testament, the theologian of grace and of the cross. His conversion is celebrated not only as his personal transformation but as the pattern of God's habit of choosing the unlikely.
conversionOfSaintPaulApostle.prayer: O God, who taught the whole world through the preaching of blessed Paul: grant that we who celebrate his conversion may follow his example and come to your presence.

saintsTimothyAndTitusBishops.name: Ss. Timothy & Titus
saintsTimothyAndTitusBishops.bio: Timothy and Titus were companions of Paul. Timothy, the son of a Greek father and Jewish mother, was circumcised by Paul for missionary purposes and served the church in Ephesus. Titus, a Gentile convert, was Paul's emissary to Corinth and the first bishop of Crete. Paul's letters to them -- the Pastoral Epistles -- are the oldest surviving documents of episcopal governance. They are remembered together because they both received letters from Paul instructing them in the care of God's people.
saintsTimothyAndTitusBishops.prayer: Lord, you guided your Church through the faithful service of Timothy and Titus. Raise up in our time bishops and pastors formed in the same school of charity.

saintAngelaMericiVirgin.name: St. Angela Merici
saintAngelaMericiVirgin.bio: Angela founded the Company of St. Ursula in Brescia in 1535 -- the first teaching order of women in the Church, dedicated to the education of poor girls. She did not establish a convent; her sisters lived in their own homes and moved freely through the city. Angela had a mystical vision in a field as a young woman that she would found a community of virgins serving God. She spent forty years preparing. She is the patron saint of the disabled, the sick, and those who have lost their parents.
saintAngelaMericiVirgin.prayer: O God, who called Angela to serve the young and the poor: raise up in our time her daughters's spirit of creative and courageous charity.

saintThomasAquinasPriestAndDoctor.name: St. Thomas Aquinas
saintThomasAquinasPriestAndDoctor.bio: Thomas was born in 1225, the son of a Norman count, educated at Monte Cassino and Naples, a Dominican friar despite his family's fierce objections, a student of Albert the Great in Cologne and Paris, the greatest systematic theologian in the history of the Church. His Summa Theologiae runs to four thousand pages and touches virtually every question of philosophy, theology, and ethics. Near the end of his life, after a mystical experience during Mass, he stopped writing. "All that I have written seems to me like straw compared to what I have seen." He died in 1274.
saintThomasAquinasPriestAndDoctor.prayer: Grant us, Lord, by the intercession of Thomas Aquinas, sharpness of mind in the study of your truth, and warmth of heart in its contemplation.

presentationOfTheLord.name: The Presentation of the Lord
presentationOfTheLord.bio: Forty days after Christmas, Mary and Joseph brought the child Jesus to the Temple in Jerusalem, as the Law required. There they encountered two figures of extraordinary antiquity: Simeon, who had been promised he would not die before seeing the Messiah, and Anna, a widow of eighty-four who had spent her life in the Temple in prayer and fasting. Simeon took the child in his arms and sang what became the Nunc Dimittis -- the canticle of Compline. The encounter of the old world with the new, of the long waiting with its fulfillment, is the image the Church meditates on this day.
presentationOfTheLord.prayer: Almighty Father, your Son was presented in the Temple and recognized as the light of the nations. May we receive him with the faith of Simeon and the devotion of Anna.

saintBlaseBishopAndMartyrSaintAnsgarBish.name: St. Blaise
saintBlaseBishopAndMartyrSaintAnsgarBish.bio: Blaise was bishop of Sebaste in Armenia, martyred in 316 AD. According to tradition, he healed a boy choking on a fishbone, and this is the origin of the blessing of throats performed on his feast day. He was a physician before becoming a bishop. The blessing of throats with crossed candles is one of the oldest sacramentals in the Western calendar. His intercession is invoked for all diseases of the throat.
saintBlaseBishopAndMartyrSaintAnsgarBish.prayer: Through the intercession of Saint Blaise, bishop and martyr, may God deliver you from ailments of the throat and from every other evil.

saintAgathaVirginAndMartyr.name: St. Agatha
saintAgathaVirginAndMartyr.bio: Agatha was a young Sicilian woman martyred around 251 AD for refusing the advances of the Roman consul Quintianus. She endured torture with extraordinary courage, and tradition says that when Saint Peter appeared to her in prison, her wounds were healed. She is the patron of those suffering from breast cancer, bellmakers, bakers, and the island of Sicily. She is one of the few women whose name has been in the Roman Canon of the Mass since at least the sixth century.
saintAgathaVirginAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who strengthened the heart of your servant Agatha against all the assaults of the enemy: grant us also the grace to overcome all adversity through love of you.

saintPaulMikiAndCompanionsMartyrs.name: Ss. Paul Miki & Companions
saintPaulMikiAndCompanionsMartyrs.bio: On February 5, 1597, twenty-six Christians -- Franciscan missionaries and Japanese converts, including three young boys -- were crucified on a hill outside Nagasaki. Paul Miki, a Jesuit scholastic, preached from his cross. He forgave his executioners. He testified to the faith that had brought him there. Japan had received the Gospel from Francis Xavier in 1549; the persecution that followed produced one of the most luminous martyrologies in the history of the Church.
saintPaulMikiAndCompanionsMartyrs.prayer: O God, who consecrated the first fruits of the faith in Japan with the blood of Paul and his companions: grant, through their intercession, that the seed they planted may continue to bear fruit.

saintJeromeEmilianiSaintJosephineBakhita.name: St. Jerome Emiliani
saintJeromeEmilianiSaintJosephineBakhita.bio: Jerome was a Venetian soldier, imprisoned by enemies at Castelnuovo in 1511. In his prison cell he promised his life to the Virgin if he were freed. He escaped, became a priest, and spent the rest of his life founding orphanages, hospitals, and schools for the poor and abandoned children of northern Italy. He died in 1537 caring for the sick during a plague, having caught the disease himself. He is the patron saint of orphans and abandoned children.
saintJeromeEmilianiSaintJosephineBakhita.prayer: Father of the orphan and defender of the poor, through the intercession of Jerome Emiliani, strengthen those who care for the abandoned.

saintScholasticaVirgin.name: St. Scholastica
saintScholasticaVirgin.bio: Scholastica was the twin sister of Benedict of Nursia. She founded a convent near Monte Cassino. Once a year the twins met at a house between their two monasteries. At their last meeting, as the evening ended and Benedict prepared to return, Scholastica prayed that he would stay. A sudden storm made it impossible for him to leave. Three days later she died. Gregory the Great tells the story to illustrate that she who loved more was the more powerful. The greater love was hers.
saintScholasticaVirgin.prayer: Lord, you drew Scholastica to yourself with so great a love that she could not be separated from you in death. Grant us a portion of her ardor.

ourLadyOfLourdes.name: Our Lady of Lourdes
ourLadyOfLourdes.bio: On February 11, 1858, a fourteen-year-old girl named Bernadette Soubirous saw a light in the grotto of Massabielle near Lourdes in the French Pyrenees. The apparitions continued eighteen times. The figure identified herself: "I am the Immaculate Conception." The spring that appeared has become one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in the world. Millions who come to Lourdes are sick. Most are not cured. All are changed by the encounter with suffering endured in faith.
ourLadyOfLourdes.prayer: O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to you. Comfort the sick, strengthen the weak, and lead all who seek you to your Son.

saintsCyrilMonkAndMethodiusBishop.name: Ss. Cyril & Methodius
saintsCyrilMonkAndMethodiusBishop.bio: Brothers from Thessaloniki, ninth-century missionaries to the Slavic peoples. Cyril created the Glagolitic alphabet -- the precursor of Cyrillic -- specifically to translate the Scriptures and liturgy into the Slavic tongue. They believed the Gospel must be heard in the language of the people, a conviction that put them in conflict with German bishops who insisted on Latin. John Paul II named them co-patrons of Europe alongside Benedict. Their mission established the Orthodox and Catholic traditions of Eastern Europe.
saintsCyrilMonkAndMethodiusBishop.prayer: God of all peoples, you sent Cyril and Methodius to give the Slavic peoples a language for your word. Bless the diversity of your Church and unite all nations in the praise of your name.

sevenHolyFoundersOfTheServiteOrder.name: The Seven Founders of the Servite Order
sevenHolyFoundersOfTheServiteOrder.bio: Seven Florentine merchants, members of a Marian confraternity, withdrew to Monte Senario in 1233 after a vision of the Virgin on the Feast of the Assumption. They became the founding community of the Order of Servants of Mary. They lived in strict poverty, spending their time in prayer, penance, and contemplation of Our Lady's sorrows. One of them, Alexis Falconieri, lived to see his order officially confirmed and died at the age of 110.
sevenHolyFoundersOfTheServiteOrder.prayer: O God, who gathered these seven holy men in devotion to the Mother of Sorrows: grant us through their intercession a share in the contemplation of the suffering that brought our redemption.

saintPeterDamianBishopAndDoctorOfTheChur.name: St. Peter Damian
saintPeterDamianBishopAndDoctorOfTheChur.bio: Peter was a monk and hermit of the eleventh century who became the most severe reformer of his age. His Liber Gomorrhianus was a blistering attack on the sexual corruption of the clergy. His Book on the Lord's Desire for Our Salvation was a meditation on the love of God. He was made Cardinal of Ostia against his will, used the office to reform monasteries across Italy, and begged repeatedly to be allowed to return to his hermitage. He died on the road in 1072, having never stopped his double work of reform and contemplation.
saintPeterDamianBishopAndDoctorOfTheChur.prayer: Lord, you gave Peter the courage to call the Church to holiness. Give us the same clear sight and the same love that is its source.

chairOfSaintPeterApostle.name: The Chair of St. Peter
chairOfSaintPeterApostle.bio: The ancient stone chair preserved in the apse of St. Peter's Basilica symbolizes the authority of the Bishop of Rome as successor to Peter. Jesus said: "Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church." This feast celebrates not merely a piece of furniture but the principle of apostolic succession -- the unbroken chain of ordained ministry reaching back through the centuries to the twelve. Whatever one makes of the papacy's history, this principle has given the Church a remarkable continuity of identity across two thousand years.
chairOfSaintPeterApostle.prayer: O Lord, who hast built your Church upon the rock of Peter's confession: grant that no flood of error may overwhelm the foundation you yourself have laid.

saintPolycarpBishopAndMartyr.name: St. Polycarp
saintPolycarpBishopAndMartyr.bio: Polycarp was bishop of Smyrna, a disciple of the Apostle John, who had himself been the beloved disciple. He was martyred in 155 AD at the age of eighty-six. His martyrdom is recorded in the first eyewitness account of a Christian martyrdom to survive. When asked to renounce Christ, he said: "For eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong. How can I blaspheme my King and Saviour?" He was burned at the stake, and when the flames did not consume him, he was stabbed. He is a link between the apostolic generation and the second century Church.
saintPolycarpBishopAndMartyr.prayer: O God, you strengthened Polycarp to hold fast to the faith received from the Apostle John. Grant us the same tenacity in love.

saintCasimir.name: St. Casimir
saintCasimir.bio: Casimir was a prince of Poland and Lithuania, third son of King Casimir IV, born in 1458. He refused a crown offered to him by Hungarian nobles, preferring prayer and fasting to political ambition. He lived austerely, sleeping on the floor, spending nights in prayer outside locked church doors. He died at twenty-five of tuberculosis. A Latin hymn to Mary -- Omni die dic Mariae -- was found in his hand after death and is still sung. He is the patron saint of Poland and Lithuania.
saintCasimir.prayer: Lord, you gave Casimir the wisdom to prefer your kingdom to all earthly crowns. Give us grace to desire what is truly lasting.

saintsPerpetuaAndFelicityMartyrs.name: Ss. Perpetua & Felicity
saintsPerpetuaAndFelicityMartyrs.bio: Perpetua was a twenty-two-year-old noblewoman, newly baptized, nursing her infant son. Felicity was her slave, pregnant, martyred eight months into her pregnancy -- she gave birth in prison two days before her death. They were executed in the arena at Carthage in 203 AD during the persecution of Septimius Severus. Perpetua's prison diary is the oldest surviving text written by a Christian woman. Her final words to her brother: "Stand fast in the faith, love one another, and do not be scandalised by our suffering."
saintsPerpetuaAndFelicityMartyrs.prayer: Father of the martyrs, you strengthened Perpetua and Felicity to choose death rather than deny you. Give us a share of their unconquerable love.

saintJohnOfGodReligious.name: St. John of God
saintJohnOfGodReligious.bio: John was a Portuguese soldier and bookseller who at the age of forty heard a sermon by John of Avila and suffered a conversion so violent that he was thought to have gone mad. He was committed to the Royal Hospital in Granada, where his care for the insane converted him to a ministry of hospitality. He founded the Brothers Hospitallers -- the Order of Saint John of God -- who still run hospitals throughout the world. He died in 1550, his health broken by years of carrying sick patients on his back.
saintJohnOfGodReligious.prayer: O God, who endowed John of God with the spirit of compassion: grant us through his intercession a heart like his, tender toward suffering wherever it appears.

saintFrancesOfRomeReligious.name: St. Frances of Rome
saintFrancesOfRomeReligious.bio: Frances was a Roman noblewoman of the fifteenth century who wished to be a nun but was married at thirteen to Lorenzo de Ponziani. She raised three children, managed a household, survived plague and war, buried two of her children, and all the while lived as though in constant prayer. For twenty-three years she was guided by an angel visible only to her. After her husband's death she joined the community of Oblates she had founded. She is the patron saint of motorists -- because her angel allegedly lit the road in front of her carriage.
saintFrancesOfRomeReligious.prayer: Lord, Frances lived as a wife, mother, and servant of the poor without ever ceasing to pray. Teach us her art of finding you in the midst of ordinary life.

saintPatrickBishop.name: St. Patrick
saintPatrickBishop.bio: Patrick was a Romano-British Christian, enslaved at sixteen by Irish raiders and taken to Ireland. He escaped, trained for the priesthood, and returned to Ireland as its bishop -- to the very country that had enslaved him. His Confessio is a document of extraordinary humility: he apologizes repeatedly for his lack of education, then proceeds to describe a life of such missionary courage and apostolic fruitfulness that the apologies read as the deepest form of pride. He converted the island. He died around 460 AD.
saintPatrickBishop.prayer: Arise today through the strength of heaven, the light of the sun, the radiance of the moon, the splendor of fire. Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me, Christ in me.

saintCyrilOfJerusalemBishopAndDoctor.name: St. Cyril of Jerusalem
saintCyrilOfJerusalemBishopAndDoctor.bio: Cyril was bishop of Jerusalem from 349 to 387 AD, with frequent interruptions for exile imposed by Arian emperors. His Catechetical Lectures -- delivered to those preparing for baptism at Easter -- are among the most complete and vivid accounts of early Christian initiation that survive. He explained the sacraments by doing them: baptism, confirmation, Eucharist. His description of first communion -- the bread and the chalice received with hands cupped like a throne -- is one of the most beautiful passages in patristic literature.
saintCyrilOfJerusalemBishopAndDoctor.prayer: Lord God, who gave Cyril the gift of explaining the mysteries of faith with clarity and warmth: grant that we may receive those mysteries with the same awe that he described.

josephHusbandOfMary.name: St. Joseph, Husband of Mary
josephHusbandOfMary.bio: Joseph is the most silent of the major figures in the Gospel. He receives angelic messages in dreams. He acts on them without recorded speech. He takes Mary as his wife, flees to Egypt, returns to Nazareth, searches for the lost boy in Jerusalem. He is called a just man. The tradition holds that he died before the public ministry of Jesus -- that he was spared the Passion that Mary witnessed. He is the patron of the universal Church, of a happy death, of workers, of fathers, of the interior life.
josephHusbandOfMary.prayer: Guardian of the Redeemer, faithful servant in silence and in darkness: teach us to act without needing to understand, and to trust without needing to see.

annunciation.name: The Annunciation of the Lord
annunciation.bio: The Angel Gabriel appeared to Mary in Nazareth. He told her she would conceive and bear the Son of God. She asked how this could be. He told her. She said: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word." In that moment -- in the yes of a young woman in an obscure village -- the Incarnation began. The Church has always read this as the hinge of human history: the moment at which God entered the creation he had made. Nine months later is December 25.
annunciation.prayer: Pour forth, we beseech thee O Lord, thy grace into our hearts; that we, to whom the Incarnation of Christ thy Son was made known by the message of an angel, may by his Passion and Cross be brought to the glory of his Resurrection.

saintJohnBaptistDeLaSallePriest.name: St. John Baptist de la Salle
saintJohnBaptistDeLaSallePriest.bio: John Baptist de la Salle was a French priest of the seventeenth century who gave up his wealth, his canonry, and his social position to found free schools for poor boys. He created the first teacher training college in history, invented the practice of teaching in French rather than Latin, and established the Brothers of the Christian Schools. He was harassed by rivals, abandoned by followers, and died in 1719 at sixty-eight, having transformed the education of the poor. He is the patron saint of teachers.
saintJohnBaptistDeLaSallePriest.prayer: O God, who gave John Baptist the zeal to educate the young and the poor: raise up in our time teachers fired with the same charity and the same patience.

saintStanislausBishopAndMartyr.name: St. Stanislaus
saintStanislausBishopAndMartyr.bio: Stanislaus was bishop of Kraków, martyred in 1079 by King Bolesław II of Poland, whom he had excommunicated for his crimes. The king killed him personally with a sword while he was celebrating Mass. He is the patron saint of Poland, and his martyrdom -- like Becket's ninety years later -- established the principle that the Church's authority extends even to kings. His relics in the Wawel Cathedral have been a site of pilgrimage and national identity for nine centuries.
saintStanislausBishopAndMartyr.prayer: Lord, you gave Stanislaus the courage to oppose royal tyranny in defense of your law. Strengthen those who speak truth to power in every age.

saintMartinIPopeAndMartyr.name: St. Martin I
saintMartinIPopeAndMartyr.bio: Martin was pope from 649 to 653, during the Monothelite controversy -- the heresy that Christ had only one will. He called the Lateran Council, which condemned the heresy. The Emperor Constans II, who supported the heresy, had him arrested, tried for treason, publicly humiliated, and exiled to Crimea, where he died of neglect and starvation in 655. His letters from exile describe not bitterness but grief that no one in Rome thought to send him bread. He is the last pope venerated as a martyr.
saintMartinIPopeAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who sustained Martin through exile and hunger: grant that we may hold the faith with his tenacity and offer our suffering with his peace.

saintAnselmOfCanterburyBishopAndDoctorOf.name: St. Anselm
saintAnselmOfCanterburyBishopAndDoctorOf.bio: Anselm was an Italian monk who became Prior of Bec in Normandy and eventually Archbishop of Canterbury -- twice exiled by English kings for defending the Church's freedom. He is called the Father of Scholasticism. His ontological argument for the existence of God -- that God is that than which nothing greater can be conceived -- has been debated by philosophers for nine centuries. His Cur Deus Homo (Why God Became Man) is the classic treatment of the theology of atonement. His prayer life was as serious as his logic.
saintAnselmOfCanterburyBishopAndDoctorOf.prayer: O God, whom to know is life, whom to seek is rest, and whom to find is all: grant that we may follow Anselm in seeking understanding through faith, and faith through love.

saintGeorgeMartyrSaintAdalbertBishopAndM.name: St. George
saintGeorgeMartyrSaintAdalbertBishopAndM.bio: George was a soldier martyred in Palestine around 303 AD during the persecution of Diocletian. Almost nothing is known about him historically, but he became one of the most venerated martyrs in both East and West. The dragon legend belongs to medieval hagiography -- an allegorization of his victory over the ancient serpent. He is the patron of England, Georgia, and soldiers. What we do know is that his courage in death impressed the generation that witnessed it so deeply that his name was remembered for seventeen centuries.
saintGeorgeMartyrSaintAdalbertBishopAndM.prayer: O God, who granted George the grace to overcome the ancient dragon of sin and death: grant us courage in every battle of the spirit.

saintFidelisOfSigmaringenPriestAndMartyr.name: St. Fidelis of Sigmaringen
saintFidelisOfSigmaringenPriestAndMartyr.bio: Mark Rey was a German lawyer who became a Capuchin friar, taking the name Fidelis (Faithful). He was assigned to preach the Counter-Reformation in the Graubünden region of Switzerland. The Calvinist community there, supported by Protestant forces, killed him in 1622 -- the first martyr of the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith. His last recorded words before being killed: "I came to plant the faith, not to take your lives."
saintFidelisOfSigmaringenPriestAndMartyr.prayer: Lord, Fidelis gave his life in faithful service to the Gospel. May his witness strengthen all who preach the faith in hostile places.

saintMarkTheEvangelist.name: St. Mark
saintMarkTheEvangelist.bio: Mark was a companion of Paul and Barnabas, cousin of Barnabas, interpreter and disciple of Peter. His Gospel -- the shortest and most vivid of the four -- was almost certainly composed in Rome and reflects Peter's preaching. The word "immediately" (euthys) appears forty-one times in his sixteen chapters. Things happen fast in Mark. Jesus acts, heals, commands, and moves on. The Church in Alexandria claims Mark as its founder. His symbol is the lion, because his Gospel opens in the wilderness with the voice of one crying out.
saintMarkTheEvangelist.prayer: O God, who exalted blessed Mark by the glory of the Gospel: grant us to be so guided by his teaching that we may follow in the footsteps of Christ.

saintPeterChanelPriestAndMartyrSaintLoui.name: St. Peter Chanel
saintPeterChanelPriestAndMartyrSaintLoui.bio: Peter was a French Marist priest, the first martyr of Oceania. He arrived on the island of Futuna in 1837. Within three years his gentle manner had won the affection of the islanders and the hostility of their king, Niuliki, whose own son had asked to be baptized. The king sent warriors to kill him in 1841. He died saying "It is well with me." The entire island converted within two years of his death. He is the patron saint of Oceania.
saintPeterChanelPriestAndMartyrSaintLoui.prayer: Lord, the blood of Peter Chanel watered the seeds of faith in Oceania. Bless the Church that grew from his sacrifice.

saintCatherineOfSienaVirginAndDoctorOfTh.name: St. Catherine of Siena
saintCatherineOfSienaVirginAndDoctorOfTh.bio: Catherine Benincasa was the twenty-third of twenty-five children, a Dominican tertiary, a mystic who bore the stigmata, a prolific letter-writer to popes and princes, and the woman who persuaded Gregory XI to return the papacy from Avignon to Rome after seventy years. She dictated her Dialogue in an ecstatic state to three secretaries simultaneously. She is a Doctor of the Church. She died at thirty-three. One of her most quoted passages: "Be who God meant you to be, and you will set the world on fire."
saintCatherineOfSienaVirginAndDoctorOfTh.prayer: O God, you enkindled the heart of Catherine with divine love and gave her wisdom to counsel the Church. Grant us through her intercession the same burning desire for your truth and your peace.

saintPiusVPope.name: St. Pius V
saintPiusVPope.bio: Antonio Ghislieri was a Dominican friar who became pope in 1566 and presided over the implementation of the Council of Trent. He reformed the breviary and the Roman Missal -- creating what became known as the Tridentine Mass -- reorganized the Roman Curia, and excommunicated Elizabeth I of England. He organized the Holy League that defeated the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto in 1571. He credited the victory to the Rosary and established October 7 as the Feast of Our Lady of the Rosary. He died in 1572.
saintPiusVPope.prayer: O God, who guided your Church through the wisdom of Pius V in a time of great turmoil: grant us leaders of equal faith and courage in our own turbulent age.

saintJosephTheWorker.name: St. Joseph the Worker
saintJosephTheWorker.bio: This feast was established by Pius XII in 1955, on the same day as International Workers Day, as a Christian response to the communist appropriation of labor as a purely economic category. Joseph worked as a carpenter. The Son of God spent thirty of his thirty-three years in a workshop, making things with his hands. The theology of work implicit in this is immense: labor is not a curse but a participation in the creativity of God, a form of prayer, a way of serving the neighbor.
saintJosephTheWorker.prayer: O God, Creator of all things, you willed that your Son should take upon himself the life of a working man. Grant that we may find in our daily work a participation in your creative love.

saintAthanasiusBishopAndDoctor.name: St. Athanasius
saintAthanasiusBishopAndDoctor.bio: Athanasius was bishop of Alexandria from 328 to 373 AD -- forty-five years in office, seventeen of them spent in exile. He was exiled five times by four different emperors for defending the Nicene definition of the divinity of Christ against Arianism. His biography of Anthony of Egypt (which he wrote from personal acquaintance) launched the monastic movement. His phrase: "God became man so that man might become God." The tradition still repeats it. He died peacefully in his bed, having outlasted every emperor who had exiled him.
saintAthanasiusBishopAndDoctor.prayer: Almighty God, you strengthened Athanasius to defend the divinity of your Son against the whole power of the Empire. Grant us his confidence in the truth entrusted to the Church.

saintsPhilipAndJamesApostles.name: Ss. Philip & James
saintsPhilipAndJamesApostles.bio: Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Peter and Andrew. When Nathanael doubted, Philip said simply: "Come and see." At the Last Supper it was Philip who said: "Lord, show us the Father, and it is sufficient for us." Jesus replied: "He that hath seen me hath seen the Father." James the Less -- distinguished from James the brother of John -- was a kinsman of the Lord and the first bishop of Jerusalem. His letter in the New Testament insists with uncomfortable directness that faith without works is dead.
saintsPhilipAndJamesApostles.prayer: O God, who gladdens us each year with the feast of your apostles Philip and James: grant that we may come through their prayers to the knowledge of the Father whom Philip sought.

05-04.name: Bl. Michael Ghebre & Companions
05-04.bio: Michael Ghebre was an Ethiopian monk of the Vincentian mission, martyred in 1855 along with Giustino De Jacobis during the persecution of Emperor Theodore II. They represent the long history of the Ethiopian Church's encounter with Rome -- complex, contested, and at its best, deeply faithful on both sides.
05-04.prayer: Lord, who sustained your martyrs in Ethiopia through the hope of resurrection: grant that their witness may bear fruit in the unity of all who bear the name of Christ.

05-10.name: St. Damien of Molokai
05-10.bio: Jozef De Veuster was a Belgian Sacred Hearts priest who volunteered to serve the leper colony on the island of Molokai in Hawaii in 1873. He stayed for sixteen years, building churches, digging graves, dressing wounds, and eventually contracting leprosy himself. When he preached his first sermon after his diagnosis, he began: "We lepers..." He died in 1889 at forty-nine. Robert Louis Stevenson, who visited Molokai, called him "a saint and a hero."
05-10.prayer: Lord, Damien gave himself completely to those whom the world had abandoned. May his witness challenge us to seek out the excluded and forgotten.

saintsNereusAndAchilleusMartyrsSaintPanc.name: Ss. Nereus & Achilleus
saintsNereusAndAchilleusMartyrsSaintPanc.bio: Nereus and Achilleus were Roman soldiers -- according to tradition, guards of the household of Domitilla -- who converted to Christianity and were martyred in the late first or early second century. They are among the earliest martyrs of Rome. An inscription placed by Pope Damasus in the fourth century above their tomb records that they threw down their weapons on the day of their baptism. "Suddenly converted, they left the work of the tyrant, threw away their shields and weapons of war, and joyfully carried the trophies of the conqueror Christ."
saintsNereusAndAchilleusMartyrsSaintPanc.prayer: O God, who strengthened Nereus and Achilleus to prefer your service to all earthly power: grant that we too may lay down whatever hinders us from following you.

ourLadyOfFatima.name: Our Lady of Fatima
ourLadyOfFatima.bio: Between May 13 and October 13, 1917, three children -- Lucia, Francisco, and Jacinta -- saw apparitions of the Virgin Mary in the fields near Fatima, Portugal, while Europe was destroying itself in the Great War. She asked for prayer, penance, and the consecration of Russia. On October 13, a crowd of seventy thousand witnessed what has been called the Miracle of the Sun. The theological weight of Fatima lies in its insistence on two things the modern world most resists: the reality of hell, and the power of the Rosary.
ourLadyOfFatima.prayer: O Mary, who appeared at Fatima to call the world to penance and prayer: convert our hearts, obtain peace for the nations, and lead all souls to God.

saintMatthiasTheApostle.name: St. Matthias
saintMatthiasTheApostle.bio: Matthias was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the Twelve. He had been a follower of Jesus from the baptism of John to the Ascension -- a witness to the entire public ministry. The casting of lots was understood as a form of prayer: letting God decide. Tradition places his mission in Judea, Cappadocia, or Ethiopia, and his martyrdom by axe. He is a saint of humility -- chosen to fill a gap, to complete a number, faithful in obscurity.
saintMatthiasTheApostle.prayer: O God, who numbered Matthias among the Apostles: grant that we may be numbered among the elect of your eternal kingdom.

05-15.name: St. Isidore the Farmer
05-15.bio: Isidore was a Spanish farmhand in Madrid, born around 1070, who ploughed other men's fields all his life and died poor. He attended Mass every morning before work. The other farmhands complained that his devotion made him late. Angels were said to plough in his place while he prayed. He is the patron of farmers and of Madrid, canonized in 1622 alongside Ignatius of Loyola, Francis Xavier, Teresa of Ávila, and Philip Neri. He and Teresa are the only Spaniards canonized that day.
05-15.prayer: Lord, Isidore found you in the furrows of the earth. Teach us to consecrate our daily work as he consecrated his.

saintBernardineOfSienaPriest.name: St. Bernardine of Siena
saintBernardineOfSienaPriest.bio: Bernardine was a Franciscan friar and the greatest popular preacher of fifteenth-century Italy. His sermons on the Holy Name of Jesus spread the IHS monogram across the Italian city-states. He declined three bishoprics. He preached across Italy for forty years, drawing crowds of ten thousand in the open air, mediating between feuding factions, reforming the Observant Franciscans. He died in 1444 at sixty-three, his voice worn out from preaching. His last sermon was delivered lying down.
saintBernardineOfSienaPriest.prayer: Lord, you gave Bernardine the gift of preaching the Holy Name with fire and joy. May the name of Jesus be always on our lips and in our hearts.

saintChristopherMagallanesAndCompanionsM.name: St. Christopher Magallanes & Companions
saintChristopherMagallanesAndCompanionsM.bio: Christopher Magallanes was a Mexican priest martyred in 1927 during the Cristero War -- the violent persecution of the Catholic Church under the anticlerical government of President Calles. He was arrested on the way to celebrate an unauthorized Mass, falsely accused of fomenting rebellion, and shot. His last words: "I die innocent, and I ask God that my blood may serve to unite my Mexican brothers." He is one of twenty-five martyrs of Mexico beatified together in 1992.
saintChristopherMagallanesAndCompanionsM.prayer: Lord, the martyrs of Mexico shed their blood rather than abandon your people. May their witness sustain the faith of all who are persecuted for your name.

saintRitaOfCascia.name: St. Rita of Cascia
saintRitaOfCascia.bio: Rita was an Augustinian nun of fifteenth-century Italy, but before she was a nun she was a wife and mother who had been forced into an arranged marriage against her will and later widowed. She asked three times to enter the convent; three times she was refused as a widow. According to tradition, she was miraculously transported inside the cloister walls. She received the stigmata of a crown of thorns. She is the patron of impossible causes, of abused wives, of widows, and of those for whom there seems to be no way forward.
saintRitaOfCascia.prayer: O God, who gave Rita grace to bear the cross of marriage, widowhood, and religious life with equal fidelity: hear through her intercession those who bring you their impossible cases.

saintBedeTheVenerablePriestAndDoctorSain.name: St. Bede the Venerable
saintBedeTheVenerablePriestAndDoctorSain.bio: Bede was an English monk of Jarrow who spent his entire life in his monastery and produced the most substantial body of scholarly work in early medieval Europe: commentaries on almost every book of the Bible, a history of the English Church and people, scientific treatises, hagiographies, hymns. His Historia Ecclesiastica Gentis Anglorum is the primary source for the history of Christianity in Britain. He died in 735 while dictating a translation of John's Gospel. His last words were the Gloria Patri.
saintBedeTheVenerablePriestAndDoctorSain.prayer: O God, who adorned your Church with the wisdom of Bede: may we, instructed by his learning and guided by his prayer, come to know you and make you known.

saintPhilipNeriPriest.name: St. Philip Neri
saintPhilipNeriPriest.bio: Philip was a Florentine who came to Rome at eighteen and lived there for sixty-five years. He spent nights in prayer in the catacombs. He heard confessions for ten hours a day. He founded the Oratory -- informal spiritual gatherings of laity and clergy that combined prayer, music, and discussion, and gave the world the oratorio musical form. His spiritual gifts included levitation, ecstasy, the reading of hearts, and an irrepressible sense of humor. He is called the Apostle of Rome and the patron saint of joy.
saintPhilipNeriPriest.prayer: O God, who never ceased to work in Philip with the fire of the Holy Spirit: grant that we may be filled with the same flame of charity and the same joy.

saintAugustineOfCanterburyBishop.name: St. Augustine of Canterbury
saintAugustineOfCanterburyBishop.bio: Augustine was a prior of a Roman monastery whom Gregory the Great sent to England in 596 to evangelize the Anglo-Saxons. He arrived afraid -- the journey was long and the people were said to be fierce. Gregory's response to his fear is famous: press on. Augustine arrived, was received by King Ethelbert of Kent, converted him, became the first Archbishop of Canterbury, and baptized ten thousand on Christmas Day 597. The English Church traces its apostolic origins to this journey.
saintAugustineOfCanterburyBishop.prayer: O God, who guided Augustine to preach the Gospel to the English people: bless through his intercession the land he evangelized and the Church he planted.

visitationOfTheBlessedVirginMary.name: The Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
visitationOfTheBlessedVirginMary.bio: After the Annunciation, Mary went in haste to the hill country to visit her cousin Elizabeth. When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the child in her womb leaped for joy. Elizabeth cried: "Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb! And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" And Mary sang the Magnificat. The scene is one of the most intimate in the Gospel: two pregnant women, a leaping infant, a canticle of praise. The first human being to recognize the presence of Christ was John the Baptist in his mother's womb.
visitationOfTheBlessedVirginMary.prayer: Almighty God, you inspired the Virgin Mary, mother of your Son, to visit Elizabeth and assist her in her need: keep us open to the working of your Spirit, and with Mary may we always magnify your holy name.

saintJustinMartyr.name: St. Justin Martyr
saintJustinMartyr.bio: Justin was a philosopher from Samaria who converted to Christianity after searching through the schools of philosophy and finding only in the Gospel the truth his reason had been seeking. He wrote two Apologies defending Christianity to the Emperor Antoninus Pius, and a Dialogue with Trypho, a Jew, which is the oldest extended piece of Christian apologetics that survives. He was beheaded in Rome around 165 AD, giving us the oldest description of a Sunday Eucharist in Christian literature.
saintJustinMartyr.prayer: O God, who guided Justin from the search of philosophy to the certainty of faith: grant that all who seek you with sincerity may find you, the Truth that all wisdom anticipates.

saintsMarcellinusAndPeterMartyrs.name: Ss. Marcellinus & Peter
saintsMarcellinusAndPeterMartyrs.bio: Marcellinus was a Roman priest and Peter an exorcist, both martyred under Diocletian around 304 AD. Constantine later built a basilica over their tomb. Their names appear in the Roman Canon of the Mass -- the oldest layer of the Eucharistic prayer -- in the list of martyrs read at every Mass. Almost nothing is known about them historically, but they have been prayed to at every Roman Rite Mass for sixteen centuries.
saintsMarcellinusAndPeterMartyrs.prayer: O God, who granted Marcellinus and Peter the crown of martyrdom: may their intercession strengthen us in the hour of trial.

saintsCharlesLwangaAndCompanionsMartyrs.name: St. Charles Lwanga & Companions
saintsCharlesLwangaAndCompanionsMartyrs.bio: Charles Lwanga and twenty-one companions -- pages and attendants at the court of King Mwanga II of Buganda -- were martyred between 1885 and 1887. Mwanga had them killed when they refused his sexual advances and for their refusal to abandon their Christian faith. Charles was burned alive at Munyonyo. He and his companions are the patron martyrs of sub-Saharan Africa. They were young men -- the eldest was forty-one, several were teenagers -- who died singing hymns.
saintsCharlesLwangaAndCompanionsMartyrs.prayer: O God, who adorned the Church in Africa with the blood of Charles and his companions: grant through their intercession that the faith they sealed with their lives may grow and flourish in our time.

saintBonifaceBishopAndMartyr.name: St. Boniface
saintBonifaceBishopAndMartyr.bio: Wynfrith of Devon was an English Benedictine monk who became the Apostle of Germany. He felled the sacred oak of the Germanic god Donar at Geismar without being struck down -- a public test of the power of the Christian God that converted the region. He organized the German Church, reformed the Frankish Church under Charlemagne's grandfather, and died at eighty in Frisia, where he had returned to evangelize, killed by pagan raiders in 754. He and his companions were reading at the time of the attack.
saintBonifaceBishopAndMartyr.prayer: Lord God, you sent Boniface to bring the Gospel to the peoples of Germany. May his courage inspire all who carry the faith to new frontiers.

saintNorbertBishop.name: St. Norbert
saintNorbertBishop.bio: Norbert was a German nobleman and canon who experienced a conversion when nearly killed by a bolt of lightning in 1115. He sold his estates, walked barefoot to Cologne in winter to be ordained a priest, and founded the Order of Premonstratensians at Prémontrée in France in 1120. The Norbertines (Canons Regular of Prémontré) combined monastic prayer with pastoral ministry. He became Archbishop of Magdeburg and worked to reconcile the papacy and the Holy Roman Empire. He died in 1134.
saintNorbertBishop.prayer: O God, who converted Norbert by a sudden calling and gave him zeal for your house: grant that we may hear your call and follow it with his wholehearted abandon.

saintEphremDeaconAndDoctor.name: St. Ephrem the Syrian
saintEphremDeaconAndDoctor.bio: Ephrem was a deacon of the Syrian Church at Edessa, the greatest Syriac writer in the tradition. His hymns -- hundreds of them -- were sung by choirs of women at liturgical celebrations and remain in the repertoire of Eastern Christianity today. He is called the Harp of the Holy Spirit. He wrote in verse because, he said, heretics used hymns to spread their errors, and the truth deserved to be sung as beautifully. He is a Doctor of the Church. He died in 373.
saintEphremDeaconAndDoctor.prayer: Pour out upon us, Lord, a portion of the spirit of prayer and praise that filled Ephrem the Syrian, that our lips too may sing of your glory and your mercy.

saintBarnabasTheApostle.name: St. Barnabas
saintBarnabasTheApostle.bio: Barnabas -- Joseph the Levite from Cyprus -- was one of the first acts of Christian generosity: he sold his field and brought the proceeds to the apostles. He introduced Paul to the Jerusalem community after his conversion, when everyone else was afraid of him. He and Paul were sent out together on the first missionary journey. They parted ways over Mark, whom Paul had dismissed and Barnabas defended. He went with Mark to Cyprus. He is called an apostle though not one of the Twelve. His feast is his monument.
saintBarnabasTheApostle.prayer: O God, who granted Barnabas the grace to see the hand of God at work in those others had rejected: grant us the same generosity of spirit.

saintAnthonyOfPaduaPriestAndDoctor.name: St. Anthony of Padua
saintAnthonyOfPaduaPriestAndDoctor.bio: Anthony was a Portuguese Augustinian canon who became a Franciscan after the bodies of the first Franciscan martyrs -- killed in Morocco in 1220 -- were brought through Coimbra. He intended to go to Africa; illness redirected him to Italy, where he encountered Francis. He became the greatest preacher of his age, preaching in the open air to crowds that no building could contain. His fame as a finder of lost things comes from a postulant who stole his psalter, had a terrifying dream, and returned it. He died in 1231 at thirty-six.
saintAnthonyOfPaduaPriestAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who gave Anthony to your people as a preacher of the Gospel and a finder of what is lost: grant that his intercession may restore to us what we most need.

saintRomualdAbbot.name: St. Romuald
saintRomualdAbbot.bio: Romuald was an Italian nobleman who witnessed his father kill a relative in a duel and retired to a Ravenna monastery in horror. He spent his life wandering the forests of Italy, founding hermitages, reforming monasteries, and seeking the absolute silence of the desert. He founded the Camaldolese -- a form of monastic life that combines the eremitical life of the hermit with the communal life of the monastery. He lived to be over a hundred. His Rule is brief: "Sit in your cell as in paradise."
saintRomualdAbbot.prayer: O God, who drew Romuald to the silence of the desert to seek your face: grant us the grace to find, in whatever silence our life permits, the same encounter.

saintAloysiusGonzagaReligious.name: St. Aloysius Gonzaga
saintAloysiusGonzagaReligious.bio: Luigi Gonzaga was the eldest son of a Mantuan nobleman, heir to the marquisate of Castiglione, who renounced his inheritance at seventeen to enter the Jesuits. He had been consecrated to the Virgin at nine and taken a vow of perpetual chastity. He died in 1591 at twenty-three, caring for plague victims in Rome. His spiritual director was Robert Bellarmine. He is the patron of Catholic youth, of those with AIDS, and of students. His discipline was severe; his charity was total.
saintAloysiusGonzagaReligious.prayer: O God, who endowed Aloysius with angelic purity of life: grant through his intercession and example that we may follow him in purity of heart.

saintPaulinusOfNolaBishopSaintsJohnFishe.name: St. Paulinus of Nola
saintPaulinusOfNolaBishopSaintsJohnFishe.bio: Paulinus was a wealthy Roman aristocrat, governor of Campania, friend of Augustine and Ambrose and Jerome. After the death of his infant son, he was baptized, gave away his vast estates to the poor, and became bishop of Nola in southern Italy. His letters are among the most affectionate in Latin literature. He is said to have sold himself into slavery to ransom a widow's son from the Vandals, then been released when the Vandal king was converted by his conversation.
saintPaulinusOfNolaBishopSaintsJohnFishe.prayer: Lord God, you moved Paulinus to abandon wealth for the love of the poor. Make us as generous with what we have been given.

birthOfJohnTheBaptist.name: The Nativity of St. John the Baptist
birthOfJohnTheBaptist.bio: John is the only saint besides Mary whose birth is celebrated as a feast (most saints are commemorated on the day of their death). He was born six months before Jesus. His birth was announced by Gabriel. His mother Elizabeth, aged and barren, conceived by God's intervention -- like Sarah before her. He preached in the desert, baptized in the Jordan, called Israel to repentance, and pointed to the Lamb of God. He died in prison, beheaded because a woman who danced pleased a king who had imprisoned him. Jesus said: "Among those born of women, there has arisen none greater than John the Baptist."
birthOfJohnTheBaptist.prayer: O God, who raised up John the Baptist to make straight the paths of your Son: grant that we who have heard his voice in the wilderness may walk in the way he prepared.

saintIrenaeusBishopAndMartyr.name: St. Irenaeus
saintIrenaeusBishopAndMartyr.bio: Irenaeus was bishop of Lyon in the late second century, born in Asia Minor, a disciple of Polycarp who was a disciple of John. He wrote Against Heresies -- a systematic refutation of Gnosticism -- and the Demonstration of Apostolic Preaching, a summary of the faith. His theology of recapitulation -- that Christ sums up and restores all that Adam lost -- is one of the most influential frameworks in Christian thought. His most quoted line: "The glory of God is man fully alive; and the life of man is the vision of God."
saintIrenaeusBishopAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who gave Irenaeus the wisdom to defend the faith against those who would make it a secret knowledge for the few: grant that we may receive the whole truth of the Gospel.

peterAndPaulApostles.name: Ss. Peter & Paul
peterAndPaulApostles.bio: Peter and Paul are the twin pillars of the Roman Church. Peter the fisherman who confessed: "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God." Paul the Pharisee who heard: "Saul, Saul, why dost thou persecute me?" They were different men -- Peter impulsive, Paul relentless; Peter from Galilee, Paul from Tarsus; Peter Jewish through and through, Paul the theologian of Gentile inclusion. Both were martyred in Rome under Nero. Both are buried in Rome. The city that killed them is identified by their names.
peterAndPaulApostles.prayer: O God, who consecrated this day with the martyrdom of your apostles Peter and Paul: grant that your Church may always follow the teaching of those through whom the faith was first planted.

firstMartyrsOfTheChurchOfRome.name: The First Martyrs of Rome
firstMartyrsOfTheChurchOfRome.bio: The Christians burned alive in the gardens of Nero in 64 AD, following the Great Fire of Rome, are the first recorded martyrs of the Roman Church. Tacitus describes them being covered in animal skins and torn apart by dogs, crucified, or set on fire to illuminate Nero's gardens at night. Their names were not recorded. They are the anonymous foundation of the Roman Church -- a community that survived by dying.
firstMartyrsOfTheChurchOfRome.prayer: God of the martyrs, you built your Church on the witness of those whose names we do not know. Remember them, and through their unknown sacrifice, sustain the faith they sealed.

saintThomasTheApostle.name: St. Thomas the Apostle
saintThomasTheApostle.bio: Thomas called Didymus -- the Twin -- said to the disciples when Jesus proposed returning to Judea: "Let us also go, that we may die with him." At the Last Supper he said he did not know where Jesus was going. After the Resurrection he was absent when Jesus appeared to the others, and refused to believe without seeing the wounds. When Jesus appeared again and invited him to touch the wounds, Thomas said: "My Lord and my God." Jesus replied: "Blessed are they that have not seen, and have believed." Thomas is the patron of those who believe through doubt.
saintThomasTheApostle.prayer: O God, who permitted Thomas to doubt so that we who come after might believe the more firmly: grant us, through his intercession, faith strong enough to confess: My Lord and my God.

saintElizabethOfPortugal.name: St. Elizabeth of Portugal
saintElizabethOfPortugal.bio: Elizabeth was queen of Portugal, wife of King Dinis, daughter of the King of Aragon. She survived an unfaithful husband, a rebellious son, two wars, and the death of her husband -- and used each experience of suffering to go deeper into prayer and charity. She built hospitals, ransomed prisoners, cared for the poor personally. She became a Franciscan tertiary after her husband's death. She died in 1336 trying to make peace between her son and his son-in-law. She is called the Peacemaker.
saintElizabethOfPortugal.prayer: Lord, Elizabeth used the power of her position entirely for the service of peace and the poor. May she intercede for peace wherever families and nations are at war.

saintMariaGorettiVirginAndMartyr.name: St. Maria Goretti
saintMariaGorettiVirginAndMartyr.bio: Maria was eleven years old when Alessandro Serenelli, a nineteen-year-old neighbor, attacked her with a knife for refusing his advances. She died the following day, having forgiven him. Alessandro was imprisoned for thirty years, converted after Maria appeared to him in a dream, and attended her canonization in 1950, sitting beside her mother. He spent the rest of his life as a lay brother in a Capuchin monastery. She is the patron of rape victims and of youth.
saintMariaGorettiVirginAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who gave Maria Goretti strength to preserve her purity unto death and to forgive her murderer: grant, through her intercession, the grace of forgiveness to all who have been wounded by violence.

saintsAugustineZhaoRongPriestAndCompanio.name: St. Augustine Zhao Rong & Companions
saintsAugustineZhaoRongPriestAndCompanio.bio: Augustine Zhao Rong was a Chinese soldier who converted to Christianity while guarding foreign missionaries being taken to martyrdom. He became a priest and was martyred in 1815 during the Jiaqing persecution. He is one of 120 martyrs of China, martyred between 1648 and 1930, canonized by John Paul II in 2000. Eighty-seven of the 120 were Chinese laypeople. Their martyrdom spans three centuries of the Church's encounter with Chinese civilization.
saintsAugustineZhaoRongPriestAndCompanio.prayer: O God, who raised up the martyrs of China as witnesses of the faith across three centuries: sustain the Church in China through their intercession.

saintBenedictOfNursiaAbbot.name: St. Benedict
saintBenedictOfNursiaAbbot.bio: Benedict of Nursia was born around 480 AD, educated in Rome, horrified by its corruption, and withdrew to a cave at Subiaco. He eventually founded Monte Cassino and wrote his Rule -- the most influential document in the history of Western monasticism. The Rule is moderate, humane, and psychologically wise in a way that still impresses. It values stability, obedience, and conversion of life. It governed the monasteries that preserved classical learning through the chaos of the early Middle Ages. Benedict is the patron of Europe.
saintBenedictOfNursiaAbbot.prayer: O God, who made blessed Benedict an outstanding guide in the school of divine service: grant that, putting nothing before love of you, we may hasten with joy along the way of your commandments.

saintHenryBishopAndMartyr.name: St. Henry
saintHenryBishopAndMartyr.bio: Henry II was Holy Roman Emperor from 1002 to 1024, a deeply devout man who used his political power in the service of Church reform. He founded the diocese of Bamberg, reformed monasteries throughout his empire, and worked with Pope Benedict VIII. He and his wife Cunigunde are both saints -- one of the few married couples in the canon. He is the patron of Benedictine oblates and of those who are handicapped.
saintHenryBishopAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who guided Henry to seek your kingdom first in the exercise of earthly power: grant that we may use whatever authority we possess in your service.

07-14.name: Bl. Kateri Tekakwitha
07-14.bio: Kateri was a Mohawk woman born in what is now New York State in 1656. Her mother was a Christian Algonquin, her father a non-Christian Mohawk chief. Smallpox at four left her disfigured and partially blind. She was baptized at twenty and had to flee her village after refusing marriage. She walked two hundred miles to the Jesuit mission at Kahnawake in Canada, where she lived a life of extreme asceticism and contemplative prayer until her death at twenty-four. At her death, witnesses reported that her disfigured face became beautiful. She is the first Native American to be canonized.
07-14.prayer: O God, you chose the flower of the Mohawks to be a lily of purity among her people: grant through Kateri's intercession that all peoples may find in your love a dignity that no suffering can take away.

saintBonaventureBishopAndDoctor.name: St. Bonaventure
saintBonaventureBishopAndDoctor.bio: Bonaventure was a Franciscan friar and theologian, contemporary and friend of Thomas Aquinas, who wrote both the official biography of Francis of Assisi and some of the most beautiful mystical theology in the tradition. His Soul's Journey into God (Itinerarium Mentis in Deum) traces the ascent of the soul through six stages of contemplation to mystical union. He is a Doctor of the Church, called the Seraphic Doctor. He died in 1274 during the Council of Lyon, where he had played a decisive role in the reunion of the Eastern and Western churches.
saintBonaventureBishopAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who inflamed the blessed Bonaventure with burning love of you: grant that we may follow his steps to union with you, the source of all light.

ourLadyOfMountCarmel.name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel
ourLadyOfMountCarmel.bio: Mount Carmel in Israel was the home of the prophet Elijah, who prayed for rain on its summit after the drought sent by God. The Carmelite Order traces its origins to a community of hermits who settled on Carmel in the twelfth century, living near a spring associated with Elijah. The Brown Scapular, associated with this feast, was received according to tradition by St. Simon Stock in 1251. Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross reformed and deepened the Carmelite tradition in the sixteenth century.
ourLadyOfMountCarmel.prayer: O God, whose servant Elijah stood before you on Mount Carmel: through the intercession of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, draw us to the summit of the mountain of prayer.

saintMaryMagdalene.name: St. Mary Magdalene
saintMaryMagdalene.bio: Mary Magdalene stands at every crucial moment of the Gospel: she is at the cross, she is at the tomb, she is the first to see the risen Christ, she is the first to proclaim the resurrection to the Apostles. For this last reason, tradition calls her the Apostle to the Apostles. She had been delivered of seven demons. She anointed the feet of Jesus with precious ointment and dried them with her hair. John Paul II elevated her from memorial to feast, calling her "the apostle of apostles" in the tradition of Bernard of Clairvaux.
saintMaryMagdalene.prayer: O God, who entrusted Mary Magdalene before all others with the news of the Resurrection: grant that we may proclaim the living Christ with the same love and the same urgency.

saintBridgetOfSwedenReligious.name: St. Bridget of Sweden
saintBridgetOfSwedenReligious.bio: Bridget was a Swedish noblewoman, married, mother of eight children, who began receiving mystical visions after the death of her husband. Her Revelations -- recorded by her confessor -- fill eight volumes. She founded the Brigittine Order. She spent the last decades of her life in Rome, calling popes and princes to reform. She was present at the deaths of two of her children: her daughter Cecilia, and her daughter Catherine, who became a saint herself. She died in Rome in 1373 and is a patron of Europe.
saintBridgetOfSwedenReligious.prayer: Lord, you gave Bridget the grace to find you in the visions of contemplation and in the demands of family life. Grant us the same wholeness.

saintCharbelMakhloufPriestAndHermit.name: St. Charbel Makhlouf
saintCharbelMakhloufPriestAndHermit.bio: Charbel was a Maronite monk of Lebanon, born in 1828, who spent sixteen years in the monastery and then twenty-three years as a hermit at the hermitage of Saints Peter and Paul near Annaya. He died in 1898 on Christmas Eve. After his burial, a brilliant light was seen around his tomb for forty-five nights. His body, found incorrupt months later, exuded a bloody sweat for years. He was canonized in 1977. He is one of the most venerated saints of Lebanon and of Eastern Christianity.
saintCharbelMakhloufPriestAndHermit.prayer: O God, who led Charbel into the silence of the hermitage and made him a sign of your presence: grant us through his intercession a hunger for the prayer that transforms.

saintJamesApostle.name: St. James the Apostle
saintJamesApostle.bio: James was the son of Zebedee, brother of John, one of the three apostles present at the Transfiguration and at Gethsemane. With John he asked to sit at the right and left hand of Jesus in his glory -- Jesus asked if they could drink his cup. James was the first of the Twelve to be martyred, beheaded by Herod Agrippa around 44 AD. His body, according to tradition, was carried to Compostela in Spain, making his shrine one of the three great pilgrimages of medieval Christianity alongside Rome and Jerusalem.
saintJamesApostle.prayer: O God, who sanctified James as the first of the Apostles to seal his witness with his blood: grant that we may follow his example in bearing our cross.

saintsJoachimAndAnne.name: Ss. Joachim & Anne
saintsJoachimAndAnne.bio: Joachim and Anne are the parents of the Virgin Mary -- the grandparents of Jesus. They are not named in the Gospels; their names come from the Protoevangelium of James, a second-century apocryphal text. What is certain from the Gospel is that Mary existed, was born of human parents, and was raised by them. The tradition has venerated them as the link between the Old Covenant and the New, as the people through whom the line of David reached its fulfillment in Mary and in Jesus.
saintsJoachimAndAnne.prayer: O God, who gave holy Joachim and Anne the honor of being the parents of the Mother of your Son: grant that we may receive, through their intercession, the salvation they prepared.

saintMartha.name: St. Martha
saintMartha.bio: Martha of Bethany was a friend of Jesus, sister of Mary and Lazarus. She complained when her sister sat at his feet while she worked alone. He replied that Mary had chosen the better part. When Lazarus died, it was Martha who ran to meet Jesus on the road and said: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you." His reply: "I am the resurrection and the life." She is the patron of innkeepers, cooks, and those who serve.
saintMartha.prayer: O God, who received the confession of faith from Martha's lips: grant that we may serve you with her diligence and confess you with her boldness.

saintPeterChrysologusBishopAndDoctor.name: St. Peter Chrysologus
saintPeterChrysologusBishopAndDoctor.bio: Peter was archbishop of Ravenna in the fifth century, called Chrysologus -- Golden-Worded -- for the beauty of his preaching. About 176 of his sermons survive, making him one of the best-documented preachers of the early Church. He wrote to the heretic Eutyches, who had appealed to him against the Council of Chalcedon: "We urge in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ that you give ready obedience to what has been written by the blessed pope of Rome, for blessed Peter, who lives and presides in his own see, provides the truth of faith to those who seek it."
saintPeterChrysologusBishopAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who gave Peter Chrysologus the golden words of preaching: grant that we may receive the word that was proclaimed with such beauty.

saintIgnatiusOfLoyolaPriest.name: St. Ignatius of Loyola
saintIgnatiusOfLoyolaPriest.bio: Íñigo Lopez de Loyola was a Basque soldier wounded at Pamplona in 1521. During his convalescence he read the lives of the saints and experienced a conversion -- discerning the difference between the consolation left by thoughts of God and the emptiness left by worldly daydreams. He made a pilgrimage to Montserrat, spent a year at Manresa in prayer, and wrote the Spiritual Exercises -- the most systematic and influential manual of discernment in the Western tradition. He founded the Society of Jesus. He died in 1556 at sixty-five.
saintIgnatiusOfLoyolaPriest.prayer: O God, who raised up Ignatius to be a soldier of your Church: grant that armed with his weapons -- prayer and discernment -- we may fight and overcome our spiritual adversaries.

saintAlphonsusMariaDeLiguoriBishopAndDoc.name: St. Alphonsus Liguori
saintAlphonsusMariaDeLiguoriBishopAndDoc.bio: Alphonsus was a Neapolitan lawyer who abandoned the law at twenty-seven after losing a case through a mistake and entered the priesthood. He founded the Redemptorists -- the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer -- to preach to the rural poor of southern Italy who had been abandoned by the clergy. His Moral Theology, his The Glories of Mary, and his The Practice of the Love of Jesus Christ made him the most widely read Catholic spiritual writer of his century. He is a Doctor of the Church.
saintAlphonsusMariaDeLiguoriBishopAndDoc.prayer: O God, who filled Alphonsus with a burning love for those abandoned by the world: grant that we may bring your consolation to those who most need to hear of your mercy.

saintJeanVianneyTheCureOfArsPriest.name: St. John Vianney
saintJeanVianneyTheCureOfArsPriest.bio: Jean-Marie Vianney was the Curé of Ars -- the village priest of a tiny French village -- from 1818 until his death in 1859. He was of modest intelligence; he failed his seminary examinations twice. What he had was holiness. People traveled from across France and Europe to have their confession heard by him. He reportedly spent sixteen to eighteen hours a day in the confessional. He was attacked regularly by a poltergeist he called "the Grappin." He is the patron of parish priests.
saintJeanVianneyTheCureOfArsPriest.prayer: O God, who gave the Curé of Ars such love for prayer and for sinners: grant that his example may draw us to seek reconciliation and to love the poor.

dedicationOfTheBasilicaOfSaintMaryMajor.name: The Dedication of the Basilica of St. Mary Major
dedicationOfTheBasilicaOfSaintMaryMajor.bio: Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome is one of the four major basilicas and the oldest church in the West dedicated to the Virgin Mary. According to tradition, the site was indicated by a miraculous snowfall on the Esquiline Hill in August 352 AD. The basilica houses the image of the Salus Populi Romani -- Health of the Roman People -- venerated since early Christian centuries. Pope Francis has visited this image before and after every pastoral journey.
dedicationOfTheBasilicaOfSaintMaryMajor.prayer: O God, who chose Mary as the dwelling place of your eternal Word: grant that in her church and through her intercession we may find the same welcome she gave to her Son.

transfiguration.name: The Transfiguration of the Lord
transfiguration.bio: On a high mountain -- Tabor, the tradition says -- Jesus was transfigured before Peter, James, and John. His face shone like the sun. His garments became white as snow. Moses and Elijah appeared beside him. A cloud overshadowed them. A voice spoke: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him." The disciples fell to the ground. When they looked up, they saw Jesus only. The Transfiguration is the event in the Gospel most explicitly concerned with what the spiritual life is moving toward: the vision of divine glory in a human face.
transfiguration.prayer: O God, who revealed your Son in the glory of his Transfiguration: strengthen our faith so that, having heard his voice, we may follow him to the glory he shared with Moses and Elijah.

saintSixtusIiPopeAndCompanionsMartyrsSai.name: St. Sixtus II & Companions
saintSixtusIiPopeAndCompanionsMartyrsSai.bio: Sixtus was pope from 257 to 258 AD, martyred during the persecution of Emperor Valerian, who forbade Christians to hold assemblies or enter cemeteries. He was seized while celebrating Mass in the Roman catacombs and executed on the spot with four deacons. His deacon Lawrence was martyred three days later. Sixtus's name appears in the Roman Canon of the Mass. His martyrdom is one of the best documented in early Christianity.
saintSixtusIiPopeAndCompanionsMartyrsSai.prayer: O God, you strengthened Sixtus and his companions to give their lives rather than cease from offering the Eucharist. Preserve in us the same devotion to the sacrifice of your Son.

saintDominicPriest.name: St. Dominic
saintDominicPriest.bio: Dominic de Guzmán was a Castilian canon regular who encountered the Cathar heresy in southern France and conceived the idea of an order of preachers -- men educated in theology, living in apostolic poverty, preaching the Gospel in the manner of the apostles. The Order of Preachers (Dominicans) was officially recognized in 1216. Dominic spent nine years preaching in Languedoc before the crusade against the Cathars drowned his work in blood. He is said to have spent his nights in prayer and his days in conversation. He died in 1221.
saintDominicPriest.prayer: O God, who made Dominic a herald of your truth: grant that his children may ever follow his example of preaching and prayer in the service of your word.

saintTeresaBenedictaOfTheCrossEdithStein.name: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein)
saintTeresaBenedictaOfTheCrossEdithStein.bio: Edith Stein was a German Jewish philosopher, assistant to Edmund Husserl, who converted to Catholicism in 1922 after reading Teresa of Ávila's autobiography in one night. She became a Carmelite nun, taking the name Teresa Benedicta of the Cross. She was arrested by the Nazis in 1942 at her convent in Echt, Netherlands, and murdered at Auschwitz-Birkenau on August 9, 1942. She is a patron of Europe and of martyrs. Her philosophical work on empathy preceded her life of martyrdom by thirty years.
saintTeresaBenedictaOfTheCrossEdithStein.prayer: God of Abraham and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, you brought Edith Stein to the knowledge of your truth and to the way of the cross: may she intercede for us who must also carry our cross.

saintLawrenceOfRomeDeaconAndMartyr.name: St. Lawrence
saintLawrenceOfRomeDeaconAndMartyr.bio: Lawrence was one of the seven deacons of Rome, martyred in 258 AD during the persecution of Valerian, three days after his pope Sixtus II. He was executed on a gridiron. According to tradition, he said to his executioners midway through: "Turn me over -- I am done on this side." This may be legend, but it captures something true about his witness: the courage that could joke in the face of death. He is the patron of librarians, archivists, and cooks.
saintLawrenceOfRomeDeaconAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who enkindled in Lawrence such a love that he burned not with the fire of his torment but with the fire of your love: grant us a share in that same fire.

saintClareVirgin.name: St. Clare of Assisi
saintClareVirgin.bio: Clare was eighteen when she ran away from her family at midnight to meet Francis of Assisi and begin a new life. She founded the Order of Poor Ladies -- the Poor Clares -- and lived in it for forty-two years, never leaving the convent of San Damiano, praying, fasting, and caring for the sick.
