She outlived Francis by twenty-seven years. She protected her convent from invading Saracen soldiers by exposing the Blessed Sacrament from the window -- they fled. She is the patron of television because she reportedly saw a distant Mass on the wall of her cell.
saintClareVirgin.prayer: O God, who led Clare by the way of poverty and contemplation: grant that we may follow her in detachment from the world and attachment to you alone.

saintsPontianPopeAndHippolytusPriestMart.name: Ss. Pontian & Hippolytus
saintsPontianPopeAndHippolytusPriestMart.bio: Pontian was pope and Hippolytus was his rival -- at one time the first antipope in Christian history -- who were both condemned to the mines of Sardinia by the Emperor Maximinus in 235 AD. In the mines they were reconciled. Both died of the harsh conditions. Hippolytus is the author of the Apostolic Tradition, the oldest complete description of a Roman Eucharistic prayer that survives, and the Apostolic Constitutions. Their reconciliation in suffering is itself a theological statement.
saintsPontianPopeAndHippolytusPriestMart.prayer: Lord God, who united Pontian and Hippolytus in the fellowship of suffering: grant that the divisions of your Church may be healed in the same spirit of charity.

saintMaximilianMaryKolbePriestAndMartyr.name: St. Maximilian Kolbe
saintMaximilianMaryKolbePriestAndMartyr.bio: Maximilian Kolbe was a Polish Franciscan priest imprisoned at Auschwitz in 1941. When the Nazis selected ten prisoners to be starved to death as reprisal for an escape, Kolbe stepped forward and asked to take the place of Franciszek Gajowniczek, a father of children. He led the men in his cell in prayer and hymns as they died, one by one. When he was the last survivor after two weeks, the guards killed him with an injection of carbolic acid. He is the patron of drug addicts, political prisoners, and those in difficult family situations.
saintMaximilianMaryKolbePriestAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who filled Maximilian Kolbe with love for you and for his neighbour: grant that his example of total self-giving may inspire in us a more generous and courageous love.

assumption.name: The Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
assumption.bio: The Assumption of Mary -- her taking up body and soul into heavenly glory at the end of her earthly life -- was defined as dogma by Pius XII in 1950. The doctrine had been held by virtually universal consensus in the Church since the early centuries; the definition made it formal. Theologically, the Assumption is the first fruit of the Resurrection applied to a human being other than Christ: the pledge and anticipation of what all the redeemed will receive at the last day. Mary in glory is the image of what the Church is destined to become.
assumption.prayer: O God, who took to yourself, body and soul, the Immaculate Virgin Mary, mother of your Son: grant that our hearts, fixed on things above, may merit to share in her glory.

saintStephenOfHungary.name: St. Stephen of Hungary
saintStephenOfHungary.bio: Stephen was the first king of Hungary, crowned on Christmas Day 1000 AD with a crown sent by Pope Sylvester II. He christianized Hungary with a combination of persuasion, force, and institutional genius -- founding bishoprics, monasteries, and parishes across the country. He survived his son's death before him and ruled for forty years, dying in 1038 on the Feast of the Assumption. He is said to have offered his kingdom to Our Lady on his deathbed, making Hungary "the kingdom of Mary."
saintStephenOfHungary.prayer: Lord God, you gave Stephen wisdom to govern and charity to serve: grant that those who lead nations may govern with justice and mercy.

saintJohnEudesPriest.name: St. John Eudes
saintJohnEudesPriest.bio: John Eudes was a French Oratorian of the seventeenth century who became the apostle of devotion to the Hearts of Jesus and Mary -- the liturgical devotions that would eventually become the feasts of the Sacred Heart and the Immaculate Heart. He founded the Congregation of Jesus and Mary (the Eudists) for the formation of priests and the Society of Our Lady of Charity for the rehabilitation of women who had been forced into prostitution. He is called the father of the devotion to the Sacred Heart.
saintJohnEudesPriest.prayer: O God, who gave John Eudes such devotion to the Hearts of Jesus and Mary: through his intercession, unite our hearts to the Heart of your Son.

saintBernardOfClairvauxAbbotAndDoctorOfT.name: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
saintBernardOfClairvauxAbbotAndDoctorOfT.bio: Bernard entered the abbey of Cîteaux at twenty-two, bringing thirty companions with him -- including several of his brothers. He founded the abbey of Clairvaux, reformed the Cistercian Order, preached the Second Crusade (a disaster he considered his personal failure), wrote on the love of God with an ardor and precision unmatched in the Latin tradition, and was the most influential churchman of the twelfth century. His sermons on the Song of Songs -- eighty-six of them -- remain among the greatest mystical writings in any language.
saintBernardOfClairvauxAbbotAndDoctorOfT.prayer: O God, who made Bernard a burning and shining light in your Church: through his intercession, fill us with the same spirit of prayer and zeal.

saintPiusXPope.name: St. Pius X
saintPiusXPope.bio: Giuseppe Sarto was a village priest who became pope in 1903. He lowered the age for First Communion to the age of reason -- overturning centuries of practice -- and decreed that children should receive frequently. He reformed the breviary and restored Gregorian chant. He condemned the theological movement called Modernism in the decree Lamentabili and the encyclical Pascendi. He died in August 1914, his health broken by the outbreak of the First World War, which he had tried to prevent. He is the patron of First Communicants.
saintPiusXPope.prayer: O God, who restored through Pius X the ancient practice of frequent communion: grant that we may receive the Eucharist with the faith he tried to safeguard.

queenshipOfBlessedVirginMary.name: The Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary
queenshipOfBlessedVirginMary.bio: Established by Pius XII in 1954, eight days after the Assumption, this memorial celebrates Mary's glory in heaven as Queen -- not by right of conquest but by grace, as the mother of the King. The Church has always understood Mary's queenship as one of service, not domination: the one who said "Behold the handmaid of the Lord" does not cease to be a handmaid in glory. She intercedes for the Church she mothered.
queenshipOfBlessedVirginMary.prayer: Grant us, Lord, who celebrate the Queenship of the Virgin Mary, to be made worthy, through her intercession and guidance, to attain the heavenly kingdom.

saintRoseOfLima.name: St. Rose of Lima
saintRoseOfLima.bio: Rose was the first person born in the Americas to be canonized. Born in Lima in 1586, she was a Third Order Dominican who modeled her life on Catherine of Siena and underwent extreme physical penances. She tended the sick and dying in a room of her parents' house that became the first hospital in South America. She had visions and suffered intense spiritual desolation -- what she called "the wars of the soul." She died at thirty-one and her funeral was attended by virtually the entire city of Lima.
saintRoseOfLima.prayer: Lord God, you drew Rose by the way of the cross into mystical union with your Son: grant us patience in aridity and trust in spiritual darkness.

saintBartholomewTheApostle.name: St. Bartholomew
saintBartholomewTheApostle.bio: Bartholomew -- probably the same person as Nathanael in John's Gospel -- was brought to Jesus by Philip. When told that Jesus of Nazareth was the one Moses wrote about, he said: "Can anything good come out of Nazareth?" Jesus saw him coming and said: "Behold a true Israelite, in whom there is no guile." He was a man of direct speech. Tradition places his mission in India and Armenia, where he was martyred by flaying. He is the patron of leather workers and of Armenia.
saintBartholomewTheApostle.prayer: O God, who strengthened Bartholomew in faith: grant that through his intercession your Church may love what he believed and preach what he taught.

saintLouisSaintJosephOfCalasanzPriest.name: St. Louis IX of France
saintLouisSaintJosephOfCalasanzPriest.bio: Louis was king of France from 1226 to 1270, the most powerful monarch in Europe. He was also, by all accounts, a genuinely holy man -- a daily hearer of Mass, a visitor of lepers, a founder of hospitals and the Sainte-Chapelle (built to house the Crown of Thorns), a reformer of justice who personally heard cases under an oak tree in the Bois de Vincennes. He led two crusades, both failures. He died of dysentery in Tunis on his second crusade, saying "Jerusalem, Jerusalem" as he died.
saintLouisSaintJosephOfCalasanzPriest.prayer: O God, who moved Louis to see his royal power as a service to your people: grant that all in authority may govern with justice, mercy, and the fear of God.

saintMonica.name: St. Monica
saintMonica.bio: Monica was a Berber woman from North Africa, the mother of Augustine. She prayed for his conversion for seventeen years while he lived with a woman without marriage, fathered a child out of wedlock, and moved through various philosophical and religious experiments. She followed him to Milan. She died in Ostia in 387, shortly after his baptism, saying: "Put this body anywhere. Don't trouble yourselves about it. I only ask this of you, that you remember me at the altar of the Lord." Her perseverance is the model of intercessory prayer.
saintMonica.prayer: God of patience and mercy, you gave Monica the grace to win her son Augustine through tears and prayer. Sustain all those who pray for the conversion of those they love.

saintAugustineOfHippoBishopAndDoctorOfTh.name: St. Augustine of Hippo
saintAugustineOfHippoBishopAndDoctorOfTh.bio: Augustine was born in 354 in Thagaste, North Africa, to a pagan father and Monica. He studied rhetoric, took a mistress, had a son, explored Manicheism, taught in Rome and Milan, heard Ambrose preach, was baptized at thirty-two, and became bishop of Hippo at forty-one. He wrote the Confessions -- the first autobiography in Western literature -- the City of God, On the Trinity, and enough other works to fill more than forty volumes. His influence on Western theology, philosophy, and literature is incalculable. He died in 430 as the Vandals besieged Hippo.
saintAugustineOfHippoBishopAndDoctorOfTh.prayer: Lord, you turned Augustine from the path of error to the truth of the Gospel. Grant that all who seek you in restless hearts may find their rest in you.

theBeheadingOfSaintJohnTheBaptistMartyr.name: The Passion of St. John the Baptist
theBeheadingOfSaintJohnTheBaptistMartyr.bio: Herod had imprisoned John because John told him it was not lawful to have his brother's wife. At a birthday banquet, the daughter of Herodias danced and pleased Herod so much that he swore to give her whatever she asked. She asked, at her mother's prompting, for the head of John the Baptist on a platter. So it was done. John was the last and greatest of the prophets. He prepared the way. He pointed to the Lamb. He died because he told a king the truth. The Church remembers his death with the same solemnity as his birth.
theBeheadingOfSaintJohnTheBaptistMartyr.prayer: Lord, you gave John the Baptist the strength to speak truth to power even at the cost of his life: grant us his courage in every season of cowardice.

saintGregoryTheGreatPopeAndDoctor.name: St. Gregory the Great
saintGregoryTheGreatPopeAndDoctor.bio: Gregory was a Roman aristocrat who became a monk, then a diplomat (papal legate in Constantinople), then abbot, then -- against his will -- pope in 590. He reformed the liturgy (Gregorian chant bears his name), organized the Church's social welfare during a plague and a flood, sent Augustine to England, wrote the Dialogues (including a life of Benedict), preached 40 homilies on Ezekiel, 22 on the Gospels, and the Moralia -- a massive commentary on Job that is one of the monuments of Christian ascetic theology. He signed his letters: "Servant of the servants of God."
saintGregoryTheGreatPopeAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who guided your Church through the wisdom of Gregory the Great: grant that we may follow his example of humble service and contemplative action.

birthOfTheBlessedVirginMary.name: The Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
birthOfTheBlessedVirginMary.bio: The Church celebrates the birth of Mary as a feast -- the first dawn before the Sun of Justice. Her birth is the beginning of the fulfillment of all the prophecies and longings of the Old Testament. Joachim and Anne were her parents. She was born in a world waiting. She would be the one through whom the waiting ended.
birthOfTheBlessedVirginMary.prayer: O God, your Virgin Mother's birth brought joy to the whole world. Grant that, just as she bore your Son into the world, so may we bear him to those around us.

saintJohnChrysostomBishopAndDoctor.name: St. John Chrysostom
saintJohnChrysostomBishopAndDoctor.bio: John was a monk of Antioch, ordained a deacon by Meletius and a priest by Flavian, and became the most celebrated preacher of the Eastern Church -- his surname Chrysostom means "golden-mouthed." He was made patriarch of Constantinople in 398 and spent the next six years reforming a corrupt clergy and rebuking the extravagance of the empress Eudoxia. She had him exiled twice. He died on a forced march in 407. His liturgy -- the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom -- is still celebrated every Sunday in the Orthodox Church.
saintJohnChrysostomBishopAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who adorned your Church with the eloquence and virtue of John Chrysostom: grant through his intercession a mouth of gold for proclaiming your truth.

theExaltationOfTheHolyCross.name: The Exaltation of the Holy Cross
theExaltationOfTheHolyCross.bio: This feast commemorates the finding of the True Cross by Saint Helena in Jerusalem around 320 AD, and the dedication of the basilica built over the site of Calvary and the Tomb by Constantine in 335. The cross -- the instrument of a slave's death -- became the sign of victory, the throne of the King of kings, the tree of life in the new paradise. Paul's words: "I resolved to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified." The Church exalts what the world despised.
theExaltationOfTheHolyCross.prayer: O God, who willed that your only-begotten Son should undergo the cross to save the human race: grant that we, who on earth have known his mystery, may merit the grace of his redemption in heaven.

ourLadyOfSorrows.name: Our Lady of Sorrows
ourLadyOfSorrows.bio: This feast is inseparable from the preceding day's. The cross could not be exalted without the woman who stood beneath it. Simeon had told her: "A sword shall pierce your own soul also." She is the Mater Dolorosa -- the Mother of Sorrows -- a figure who has given form to human grief for two thousand years. The Stabat Mater, composed in the thirteenth century, is among the most frequently set texts in Western music. She is the model of how suffering can be borne -- not stoically, but in faith.
ourLadyOfSorrows.prayer: O God, who willed that at the hour of salvation a sword of grief should pierce the soul of the Virgin Mary: grant that we who honor her sorrows may obtain the happy fruit of your passion.

saintsCorneliusPopeAndCyprianBishopMarty.name: Ss. Cornelius & Cyprian
saintsCorneliusPopeAndCyprianBishopMarty.bio: Cornelius was pope from 251 to 253, Cyprian bishop of Carthage from 248 to 258. Both died as a result of the persecutions under Valerian -- Cornelius in exile, Cyprian by beheading. Both were principals in the Novatianist controversy: Novatian taught that those who had lapsed under persecution could never be readmitted to the Church; Cornelius and Cyprian -- who had himself fled during the Decian persecution -- taught the mercy of re-admission after penance. Cyprian's treatise On the Unity of the Church is the first systematic ecclesiology in Christian history.
saintsCorneliusPopeAndCyprianBishopMarty.prayer: O God, who granted Cornelius and Cyprian the prize of martyrdom: grant us, through their intercession, to remain united in faith and love.

saintRobertBellarmineBishopAndDoctor.name: St. Robert Bellarmine
saintRobertBellarmineBishopAndDoctor.bio: Robert Bellarmine was a Jesuit cardinal, the greatest controversialist theologian of the Counter-Reformation, spiritual director of Aloysius Gonzaga, and a man who gave away his personal wealth to the poor. He was the judge in the case of Galileo -- twice: in 1616 he told Galileo that the heliocentric theory could not be held as fact; Bellarmine knew the difference between a theory and a demonstrated truth. He wrote the Catechism of Christian Doctrine that was used across the Catholic world for three centuries.
saintRobertBellarmineBishopAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who gave Robert Bellarmine both the strength of argument and the tenderness of charity: grant us the wisdom to hold the faith firmly and to speak it with love.

saintJanuariusBishopAndMartyr.name: St. Januarius
saintJanuariusBishopAndMartyr.bio: Januarius was bishop of Benevento, martyred under Diocletian around 305 AD. He is the patron saint of Naples. A phial of what is claimed to be his dried blood, preserved in the cathedral of Naples, liquefies three times a year on his feast days. The phenomenon has been observed since 1389 and has no scientific explanation that has achieved consensus. Whether the liquefaction is miraculous or natural, the devotion it has sustained in the people of Naples for six centuries is undeniable.
saintJanuariusBishopAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who granted Januarius the grace of martyrdom: through his intercession, strengthen our faith in the God who surpasses our understanding.

saintAndrewKimTaegonPriestAndPaulChongHa.name: Ss. Andrew Kim Tae-gon, Paul Chong Ha-sang & Companions
saintAndrewKimTaegonPriestAndPaulChongHa.bio: Korea received Christianity entirely through the witness of laypeople -- there were no missionaries. A group of Korean Catholics brought back Christian texts from Beijing in the eighteenth century and formed the first Christian community in Korea without clergy. Their descendants, persecuted in four waves between 1839 and 1867, produced 103 martyrs canonized by John Paul II in Seoul in 1984. Andrew Kim Tae-gon was the first Korean priest; he was beheaded at twenty-five.
saintAndrewKimTaegonPriestAndPaulChongHa.prayer: O God, who built your Church in Korea through the witness of laypeople and the blood of martyrs: grant that our faith may bear the same quality of testimony.

saintMatthewApostleAndEvangelist.name: St. Matthew
saintMatthewApostleAndEvangelist.bio: Matthew was a tax collector -- a member of the most despised profession in first-century Judea, a collaborator with the Roman occupation. Jesus walked past his tax booth and said: "Follow me." He rose and followed. The Gospel of Matthew, written for a Jewish-Christian community, is the most cited Gospel in the early Church, the one that begins the New Testament. Matthew is the patron of tax collectors, accountants, and bankers.
saintMatthewApostleAndEvangelist.prayer: O God, who called Matthew from his counting table to the school of your grace: grant us the same readiness to leave our securities and follow you.

saintPioOfPietrelcinaPadrePioPriest.name: St. Pius of Pietrelcina (Padre Pio)
saintPioOfPietrelcinaPadrePioPriest.bio: Francesco Forgione was a Capuchin friar from Pietrelcina in southern Italy who bore the visible wounds of Christ in his hands, feet, and side from 1918 until his death in 1968. He spent sixteen to nineteen hours a day in the confessional. Reports of bilocation, the reading of consciences, miraculous healings, and extraordinary spiritual gifts surrounded him throughout his life. He founded a hospital -- the Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza (Home for the Relief of Suffering) -- that still operates as one of the finest medical centers in Italy.
saintPioOfPietrelcinaPadrePioPriest.prayer: O God, who conformed Padre Pio to your crucified Son and gave him the gift of compassion for sinners: grant through his intercession that we may be united to the cross that saves.

saintsCosmasAndDamianMartyrs.name: Ss. Cosmas & Damian
saintsCosmasAndDamianMartyrs.bio: Cosmas and Damian were twin brothers, physicians from Syria, martyred in the early fourth century under Diocletian. They are said to have practiced medicine without payment -- anargyroi, the silverless ones -- serving the poor freely. They are the patrons of physicians, pharmacists, and surgeons. Their names appear in the Roman Canon of the Mass. Their intercession has been invoked by the sick for seventeen centuries.
saintsCosmasAndDamianMartyrs.prayer: O God, who adorned the physicians Cosmas and Damian with the palm of martyrdom: through their intercession, bless those who care for the sick with healing hands and hearts.

saintVincentDePaulPriest.name: St. Vincent de Paul
saintVincentDePaulPriest.bio: Vincent de Paul was a French priest who spent his early years anxious for preferment and haunted by a period of captivity as a slave in Tunis. After a second conversion in 1617, he devoted himself entirely to the rural poor. He founded the Congregation of the Mission (Vincentians) and, with Louise de Marillac, the Daughters of Charity -- the first women's religious congregation to work outside the cloister. He organized relief for prisoners, galley slaves, foundlings, and the victims of wars. He is the patron of charitable organizations.
saintVincentDePaulPriest.prayer: O God, who gave Vincent the grace to imitate your Son in preaching the Gospel to the poor: grant through his intercession that we may love the poor with his practical and inventive charity.

saintWenceslausMartyrSaintsLawrenceRuizA.name: St. Wenceslaus
saintWenceslausMartyrSaintsLawrenceRuizA.bio: Wenceslaus was duke of Bohemia from 921 to 929, a Christian ruler who promoted the faith in a pagan land. He was murdered by his brother Boleslav, who then found himself unable to rule a people who venerated his brother as a saint. The popular carol "Good King Wenceslas" reflects a historical reality: he was known for personal acts of charity to the poor in the depth of winter. He is the patron saint of the Czech Republic.
saintWenceslausMartyrSaintsLawrenceRuizA.prayer: Lord, you gave Wenceslaus the courage to witness to the faith in life and in death. May his intercession sustain the faith of the people he loved.

saintsMichaelGabrielAndRaphaelArchangels.name: Ss. Michael, Gabriel & Raphael
saintsMichaelGabrielAndRaphaelArchangels.bio: Michael -- "Who is like God?" -- is the warrior angel, the leader of the heavenly armies, the guardian of Israel, the weigher of souls at the last judgment. Gabriel -- "God is my strength" -- is the messenger, the one who announced the Incarnation to Mary and the birth of John the Baptist to Zechariah. Raphael -- "God heals" -- is the angel of healing, the guide of Tobias, the guardian of pilgrims. The three archangels named in Scripture are celebrated together as representatives of the entire angelic court.
saintsMichaelGabrielAndRaphaelArchangels.prayer: O God, who order the ministry of angels and of men with wonderful harmony: grant that those who always stand before you in heaven may protect our lives on earth.

saintJeromePriestAndDoctor.name: St. Jerome
saintJeromePriestAndDoctor.bio: Jerome was the greatest linguist of the early Church -- fluent in Latin, Greek, and Hebrew -- and the translator of the Bible into Latin: the Vulgate, which remained the standard biblical text of Western Christianity for fifteen hundred years. He was irascible, combative, and mercilessly self-critical. His letters are among the most vivid documents of the late fourth century. He spent the last thirty-five years of his life in a cave in Bethlehem, translating and commenting on Scripture, with a community of women scholars he had trained in Rome. He died in 420.
saintJeromePriestAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who gave Jerome a burning love for your word: grant that your people may be nourished by the sacred Scriptures and grow in knowledge and love of you.

saintThereseOfTheChildJesusVirginAndDoct.name: St. Thérèse of the Child Jesus
saintThereseOfTheChildJesusVirginAndDoct.bio: Thérèse Martin was born in Normandy in 1873 and entered the Carmelite convent at Lisieux at fifteen, dying of tuberculosis at twenty-four. She wrote her autobiography -- The Story of a Soul -- at her prioress's request. It became one of the most widely read books in Christian history. Her "little way" -- the way of spiritual childhood, of doing small things with great love, of trusting entirely in God's mercy -- has been received as one of the most significant spiritual discoveries of the modern era. She is a Doctor of the Church.
saintThereseOfTheChildJesusVirginAndDoct.prayer: O God, who opened the kingdom of heaven to little ones: grant that by following Thérèse in her little way, we may know the confidence that comes from being loved as a child.

guardianAngels.name: The Holy Guardian Angels
guardianAngels.bio: Jesus said: "See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I say to you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven." The Church has always understood this to teach that each human being has a guardian angel -- a personal messenger and protector assigned by God. The Guardian Angels are not named in Scripture but their ministry is pervasive throughout both Testaments: angels strengthen, guide, protect, announce, and accompany.
guardianAngels.prayer: O God, who in your divine providence assign holy angels to guard us: grant that we may always be guarded by their protection and rejoice with them for ever.

saintFrancisOfAssisi.name: St. Francis of Assisi
saintFrancisOfAssisi.bio: Giovanni di Pietro di Bernardone was the son of a wealthy cloth merchant. At twenty-five, following a conversion illness and an encounter with a leper whose hand he kissed, he heard Christ speak to him from the crucifix at San Damiano: "Francis, go and repair my house, which is falling into ruin." He rebuilt it literally, then spiritually -- founding the Order of Friars Minor (the Franciscans), writing the Canticle of the Creatures, and receiving the stigmata on Mount La Verna in 1224. He died in 1226, calling death "Sister." He is the patron of ecology, of animals, and of Italy.
saintFrancisOfAssisi.prayer: O God, who gave Francis the grace to imitate your Son in poverty and humility: grant that we may follow his example and be joyfully united to you through creation.

saintBrunoPriest.name: St. Bruno
saintBrunoPriest.bio: Bruno was a distinguished master of theology at Reims who founded the Carthusians -- the strictest monastic order in the Church -- at the Grande Chartreuse in the Alps in 1084. He had been deeply involved in the reform of the Church when he withdrew. He spent his last years in Calabria, in another hermitage. He never wrote a Rule; the silence of the Carthusians is itself their rule. Their motto: Stat Crux dum volvitur orbis. The cross stands while the world turns.
saintBrunoPriest.prayer: O God, who called Bruno to seek you in silence and solitude: grant that in the noise of our lives we may find the interior desert where you are heard.

ourLadyOfTheRosary.name: Our Lady of the Rosary
ourLadyOfTheRosary.bio: This feast was established by Pius V after the naval victory of Lepanto on October 7, 1571, which he credited to the Rosary being prayed throughout Europe. The Rosary is a form of meditation on the life of Christ in company with Mary: each decade of Hail Marys accompanies a mystery -- Joyful, Luminous, Sorrowful, Glorious. The prayer is simultaneously Marian and Christological. John Paul II called it "a summary of the Gospel." The simplicity of the repeated words creates the silence in which the mysteries are contemplated.
ourLadyOfTheRosary.prayer: O God, whose only-begotten Son has purchased for us the rewards of eternal life: grant, we beseech thee, that meditating upon these mysteries in the most holy Rosary, we may imitate what they contain.

saintDenisAndCompanionsMartyrsSaintJohnL.name: St. Denis & Companions
saintDenisAndCompanionsMartyrsSaintJohnL.bio: Denis was the first bishop of Paris, martyred around 258 AD during the persecution of Valerian. According to tradition, after his beheading on Montmartre -- the Hill of Martyrs -- he walked two miles to the place of his burial carrying his head and singing psalms. He is the patron of France. The legend of Denis is a study in how the tradition transformed historical memory into theological statement: the martyr continues to speak even after the executioner has done his work.
saintDenisAndCompanionsMartyrsSaintJohnL.prayer: O God, who strengthened Denis and his companions in their testimony: grant us courage to speak and act for the faith in our own generation.

saintCallistusIPopeAndMartyr.name: St. Callistus I
saintCallistusIPopeAndMartyr.bio: Callistus was pope from 217 to 222, a man of complicated background -- a former slave, implicated in financial scandals before his conversion, a deacon under Zephyrinus, then pope. He was attacked fiercely by Hippolytus, his theological rival. He extended mercy to apostates, recognized marriages between free and slave women that Roman law did not recognize, and readmitted to communion those who had committed serious sins after penance. He died, possibly in a popular uprising, in 222. His catacombs -- the Catacomb of Callistus -- are the burial place of many popes.
saintCallistusIPopeAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who gave Callistus the courage to extend your mercy beyond what prudence counseled: grant us a portion of his boldness in forgiving.

saintTeresaOfJesusVirginAndDoctorOfTheCh.name: St. Teresa of Jesus (Ávila)
saintTeresaOfJesusVirginAndDoctorOfTheCh.bio: Teresa Sánchez de Cepeda Dávila y Ahumada entered the Carmelite Convent of the Incarnation in Ávila at twenty-one and was miserable for twenty years. At thirty-nine she experienced a definitive conversion before an image of the wounded Christ. She spent the rest of her life in ecstatic prayer, founding seventeen reformed Carmelite convents across Spain, writing the Interior Castle and the Way of Perfection, collaborating with John of the Cross on the reform of the friars, and managing logistics, finances, and personnel across a network of monasteries. She is a Doctor of the Church.
saintTeresaOfJesusVirginAndDoctorOfTheCh.prayer: O God, who gave Teresa of Jesus a burning thirst for your glory and the souls of your people: grant that we, nourished by her heavenly teaching, may be inflamed with the same desire.

saintHedwigReligiousSaintMargaretMaryAla.name: St. Hedwig
saintHedwigReligiousSaintMargaretMaryAla.bio: Hedwig was duchess of Silesia in the thirteenth century, wife of Henry I, mother of seven. She used her considerable wealth to build monasteries and hospitals, to ransom prisoners and release serfs, and to care personally for the poor and the sick. After her husband's death she entered the Cistercian monastery she had founded at Trebnitz. She walked barefoot even in winter, carrying her shoes rather than wearing them. She is the patron of those who have lost their children and of those in unhappy marriages.
saintHedwigReligiousSaintMargaretMaryAla.prayer: O God, who gave Hedwig the grace to turn the authority of a princess entirely into service of the poor: grant us the same conversion of power into charity.

saintIgnatiusOfAntiochBishopAndMartyr.name: St. Ignatius of Antioch
saintIgnatiusOfAntiochBishopAndMartyr.bio: Ignatius was bishop of Antioch, arrested during the reign of Trajan and sent to Rome to be executed in the arena around 107 AD. During the journey he wrote seven letters -- to the churches of Ephesus, Magnesia, Tralles, Rome, Philadelphia, and Smyrna, and to Polycarp. In his letter to the Romans he pleaded not to be rescued: "Allow me to be eaten by the beasts, through whom I can attain to God. I am God's wheat, and I am to be ground by the teeth of wild beasts, so that I may become pure bread of Christ." The language of the Eucharist becomes the language of his martyrdom.
saintIgnatiusOfAntiochBishopAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who filled Ignatius of Antioch with a desire for martyrdom and a vision of the Church as the body of Christ: grant through his teaching that we may understand the mystery of the Eucharist with his depth.

saintLukeTheEvangelist.name: St. Luke
saintLukeTheEvangelist.bio: Luke was a physician, a Gentile, a companion of Paul, and the author of the third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles -- the longest single contribution to the New Testament. His Gospel is the Gospel of mercy: the prodigal son, the good Samaritan, the lost sheep, the penitent thief, Zacchaeus, and the weeping women of Jerusalem are all found only in Luke. He is the patron of physicians, artists, and butchers. An early tradition says he painted the first icon of the Virgin Mary.
saintLukeTheEvangelist.prayer: O God, who chose Luke the physician to reveal your love for the sick and the sinful: grant that we may follow the Christ he described -- the physician of bodies and souls.

saintsJeanDeBrebeufAndIsaacJoguesPriests.name: Ss. John de Brébeuf, Isaac Jogues & Companions
saintsJeanDeBrebeufAndIsaacJoguesPriests.bio: The North American Martyrs were eight Jesuit missionaries -- six priests and two laybrothers -- killed by the Iroquois and Mohawks between 1642 and 1649 in what is now upstate New York and Ontario. Isaac Jogues had already had his fingers chewed off in a previous captivity; when he returned to the mission, the Dutch Reformed minister who had helped rescue him could not understand why he was going back. Jogues replied that he was going to die. John de Brébeuf sang hymns as he was tortured. They are the patron saints of Canada.
saintsJeanDeBrebeufAndIsaacJoguesPriests.prayer: O God, you called John de Brébeuf and his companions to preach the Gospel and to suffer for it: grant through their intercession that the faith they planted may continue to grow.

popeSaintJohnPaulII.name: St. John Paul II
popeSaintJohnPaulII.bio: Karol Józef Wojtyła was born in Wadowice, Poland in 1920, ordained a priest in 1946, made bishop in 1958, cardinal in 1967, and elected pope on October 16, 1978 -- the first non-Italian pope since 1523. He visited 129 countries, met with world leaders, canonized 482 saints, wrote 14 encyclicals, 15 apostolic exhortations, and a full corpus of theology of the body. He survived an assassination attempt in 1981. He suffered from Parkinson's disease in his last decade and died on April 2, 2005. One million people came to Rome for his funeral.
popeSaintJohnPaulII.prayer: O God, who chose John Paul II to strengthen the faith throughout the world: grant through his intercession that we may open wide the doors of our hearts to Christ.

saintJohnOfCapistranoPriest.name: St. John of Capistrano
saintJohnOfCapistranoPriest.bio: John was a Franciscan friar, a lawyer turned preacher, who at the age of seventy led the crusade that relieved the siege of Belgrade in 1456 -- the Ottoman advance that would have opened central Europe to conquest. He died shortly after the victory, possibly of plague. He is the patron of military chaplains. His preaching missions across Europe in the early fifteenth century produced mass conversions and the establishment of Monte di Pietà -- public loan houses for the poor, precursors of modern credit unions.
saintJohnOfCapistranoPriest.prayer: O God, who sustained John of Capistrano in his old age with a young man's courage: grant that we may serve you with equal energy in whatever season of life we find ourselves.

saintAnthonyMaryClaretBishop.name: St. Anthony Mary Claret
saintAnthonyMaryClaretBishop.bio: Anthony Claret was a Spanish Catalan priest who founded the Claretians (Missionary Sons of the Immaculate Heart of Mary) in 1849. He became archbishop of Santiago de Cuba and then confessor to Queen Isabella II, using his proximity to power entirely in the service of the poor. He is said to have preached over 25,000 sermons and confirmed over 100,000 people. He survived eleven assassination attempts. He died in exile in France in 1870.
saintAnthonyMaryClaretBishop.prayer: O God, who endowed Anthony Claret with ardent zeal for the salvation of souls: grant through his intercession that the same fire of charity may burn in us.

saintsSimonAndJudeApostles.name: Ss. Simon & Jude
saintsSimonAndJudeApostles.bio: Simon the Zealot -- probably a member of the revolutionary nationalist party -- and Jude Thaddaeus (distinguished from Judas Iscariot) are celebrated together because tradition links them in their missionary journey and martyrdom, possibly in Persia. Jude is the patron of hopeless cases -- perhaps because his name was avoided by petitioners who confused him with Judas, so he was available for the desperate causes no one else would take. The brief letter of Jude in the New Testament warns against those who "pervert the grace of God into licentiousness."
saintsSimonAndJudeApostles.prayer: O God, who made Simon and Jude worthy to be called to the apostolic dignity: grant through their intercession that we may hold fast to the faith they proclaimed.

allSaints.name: All Saints
allSaints.bio: All Saints is the feast of the communion of saints in its completeness -- not only those who have been canonized, not only those whose names we know, but the entire multitude that no man can number. The Book of Revelation speaks of a great crowd from every nation, tribe, people, and language, standing before the throne. They have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb. They are our brothers and sisters who have reached the destination toward which we are still traveling.
allSaints.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, by whose gift we venerate in one celebration the merits of all the Saints: bestow on us, we pray, through the prayers of so many intercessors, an abundance of the reconciliation with you for which we earnestly long.

allSouls.name: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed
allSouls.bio: All Souls Day is the Church's annual act of intercession for the dead. The theology behind it is simple: the Church does not abandon her members at death. The dead who are still being purified -- still in the process of becoming fully what God created them to be -- receive the benefit of the Church's prayer. The practice of praying for the dead is ancient; 2 Maccabees records it. The Council of Florence and the Council of Trent defined it. Every November 2, the Church says to the dead: we have not forgotten you.
allSouls.prayer: O God, the glory of the faithful and the life of the just, by the death and resurrection of whose Son we have been redeemed: look mercifully on the souls of all the faithful departed and grant them a share in the passover of your Son.

saintCharlesBorromeoBishop.name: St. Charles Borromeo
saintCharlesBorromeoBishop.bio: Charles Borromeo was a Milanese cardinal who could have been a comfortable Renaissance prince-bishop but instead became the architect of the Counter-Reformation in northern Italy. He implemented the Council of Trent in his diocese with extraordinary thoroughness: reforming the liturgy, founding seminaries, visiting every parish, caring personally for the poor during the plague of 1576. He died at forty-six, completely worn out. He is the model of the modern bishop: pastoral, administrative, ascetic, and completely dedicated to the reform of the Church through the reform of himself.
saintCharlesBorromeoBishop.prayer: O God, who made Charles Borromeo a great shepherd to renew the face of your Church: grant us shepherds formed in the same school of sacrifice and prayer.

dedicationOfTheLateranBasilica.name: The Dedication of the Lateran Basilica
dedicationOfTheLateranBasilica.bio: The Basilica of Saint John Lateran is the cathedral of Rome -- the mother church of all the churches in the world. Its dedication is celebrated as a feast of the universal Church because it symbolizes the unity of the Church with Rome and with the successor of Peter. The inscription on the façade: "Mother and Head of all the churches of the city and the world." The Lateran was given to the Church by Emperor Constantine and has been the site of five ecumenical councils.
dedicationOfTheLateranBasilica.prayer: O God, who every year bring back the day of this church's consecration: hear the prayers of your people and grant that in your holy house all who seek your grace may find it.

saintLeoTheGreatPopeAndDoctor.name: St. Leo the Great
saintLeoTheGreatPopeAndDoctor.bio: Leo was pope from 440 to 461 -- one of the two popes called "the Great" by the tradition (the other being Gregory). He met Attila the Hun outside Rome in 452 and persuaded him to turn back -- an event so improbable that it was remembered for centuries as miraculous. His Tome -- a letter to the Council of Chalcedon -- defined the two natures of Christ with such precision that the Council fathers cried out: "Peter has spoken through Leo." He is a Doctor of the Church.
saintLeoTheGreatPopeAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who never allow your Church to be overcome by the gates of hell: grant through the teaching and intercession of Leo the Great that she may stand firm on the rock of Peter's confession.

saintMartinOfToursBishop.name: St. Martin of Tours
saintMartinOfToursBishop.bio: Martin was a Roman soldier from Pannonia who, at eighteen, meeting a freezing beggar at the gate of Amiens, cut his military cloak in two and gave half to the beggar. That night he dreamed of Christ wearing the half-cloak and saying to his angels: "Martin, who is still but a catechumen, has covered me with this garment." He was baptized. He served two more years in the army, then became a disciple of Hilary of Poitiers, a hermit, and eventually bishop of Tours -- the most popular saint of the Middle Ages in the West.
saintMartinOfToursBishop.prayer: O God, who saw Martin clothe your Son in the person of a beggar: grant that we may recognize your Son in those who come to us in need.

saintJosaphatBishopAndMartyr.name: St. Josaphat
saintJosaphatBishopAndMartyr.bio: John Kuntsevych was a Ukrainian Greek Catholic bishop of Polotsk martyred in 1623 -- the first Eastern Catholic to be canonized by Rome. He was killed by an Orthodox mob that accused him of seizing their churches. His martyrdom was in the cause of union between the Eastern and Western Churches -- a union he pursued with great pastoral zeal and with which he died in peace.
saintJosaphatBishopAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who filled Josaphat with such pastoral charity that he laid down his life for his people: through his intercession, hasten the day when all who share one baptism may be united in one faith.

saintAlbertTheGreatBishopAndDoctor.name: St. Albert the Great
saintAlbertTheGreatBishopAndDoctor.bio: Albert of Cologne was a Dominican friar and the teacher of Thomas Aquinas. He was the first medieval thinker to make a systematic study of Aristotle's natural philosophy and to integrate it with Christian theology -- the project that Thomas completed. He wrote on physics, chemistry, astronomy, biology, geography, and theology. He is the patron of scientists and of students of the natural sciences. He died in 1280 at approximately eighty years of age.
saintAlbertTheGreatBishopAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who made Albert great in learning and in holiness: grant that we may follow him in seeking wisdom with open minds and devoted hearts.

saintMargaretOfScotlandSaintGertrudeTheG.name: St. Margaret of Scotland
saintMargaretOfScotlandSaintGertrudeTheG.bio: Margaret was an Anglo-Saxon princess who fled to Scotland after the Norman Conquest and married the Scottish king Malcolm III. She used her position to reform the Scottish Church, found monasteries, ransom English slaves, and care for the poor. She introduced the practice of saying grace before meals to Scotland and improved the conditions of prisoners. She died in 1093, three days after hearing of her husband's death in battle. She is the patron saint of Scotland and of queens.
saintMargaretOfScotlandSaintGertrudeTheG.prayer: O God, who gave Margaret the grace to make her royal power serve the poor: may her intercession sustain those in authority who seek to govern with justice and charity.

saintElizabethOfHungary.name: St. Elizabeth of Hungary
saintElizabethOfHungary.bio: Elizabeth was a princess of Hungary married at fourteen to Ludwig IV of Thuringia, whom she loved deeply and who loved her. He died on crusade in 1227. She was twenty. She was expelled from the palace by her brother-in-law, found a protector in Conrad of Marburg (who was severe to the point of cruelty), founded a hospital in Marburg, and cared personally for the sick until her death at twenty-four. Her life of heroic charity in the brief years after her husband's death has made her one of the most beloved saints in the German and Franciscan traditions.
saintElizabethOfHungary.prayer: O God, who transformed Elizabeth into a living image of the suffering Christ: grant that through her intercession we may serve Christ in the poor with the same totality of love.

dedicationOfTheBasilicasOfSaintsPeterAnd.name: The Dedication of the Basilicas of Peter & Paul
dedicationOfTheBasilicasOfSaintsPeterAnd.bio: The basilicas of Saint Peter in the Vatican and Saint Paul Outside the Walls -- the burial places of the two great apostles of Rome -- were both consecrated on November 18. Their joint commemoration expresses what their joint feast on June 29 expresses: Peter and Paul are inseparable as the foundation of the Roman Church, the pillars of its faith, the martyrs whose blood planted the Gospel in the capital of the ancient world.
dedicationOfTheBasilicasOfSaintsPeterAnd.prayer: O God, who consecrated these basilicas to the memory of your apostles: grant that through the intercession of Peter and Paul we may always receive your mercy.

presentationOfTheBlessedVirginMary.name: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
presentationOfTheBlessedVirginMary.bio: This feast, celebrated in the East since the sixth century and in the West since the fourteenth, commemorates the presentation of the child Mary in the Temple by her parents Joachim and Anne -- an event recorded in the Protoevangelium of James rather than the canonical Gospels. The theological content is clear: the one who was chosen from the beginning to bear the Word of God was herself offered to God from the beginning. The Temple that received her became the dwelling place of the one who would dwell in her.
presentationOfTheBlessedVirginMary.prayer: O God, who willed that the Blessed Virgin Mary should be presented in the Temple when still a child: through her prayers grant that we too may be presented to you with pure hearts.

saintCeciliaVirginAndMartyr.name: St. Cecilia
saintCeciliaVirginAndMartyr.bio: Cecilia was a Roman martyr of the second or third century. She is one of the most venerated martyrs of the early Church, her name in the Roman Canon. The story of her martyrdom -- suffocation in her bath, then a botched decapitation that left her alive for three days, during which she prayed and directed the building of a church -- is legendary but has been told continuously since the fifth century. She is the patron of musicians, based on a passage in her Acts describing her singing to God while the wedding music played.
saintCeciliaVirginAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who gave Cecilia the gift of music and the grace of martyrdom: grant that through her intercession we may praise you always, in life and in death.

saintClementIPopeAndMartyrSaintColumbanR.name: St. Clement I
saintClementIPopeAndMartyrSaintColumbanR.bio: Clement was the fourth bishop of Rome (or third, depending on the count), serving around 88 to 99 AD. His letter to the Corinthian church -- written to address disorder in that community -- is the earliest Christian document outside the New Testament and the first exercise of Roman pastoral authority outside Rome. It establishes, in practice if not in theory, the principle of Roman intervention in another church's affairs. Tradition records him as a martyr, but this is uncertain.
saintClementIPopeAndMartyrSaintColumbanR.prayer: O God, who guided your Church through the pastoral wisdom of Clement: grant us leaders formed in the same spirit of fraternal correction and deep charity.

saintAndrewDungLacAndCompanionsMartyrs.name: Ss. Andrew Dũng-Lạc & Companions
saintAndrewDungLacAndCompanionsMartyrs.bio: Andrew Dũng-Lạc was a Vietnamese priest martyred in 1839 under Emperor Minh Mạng. He is one of 117 martyrs of Vietnam -- bishops, priests, and laypeople martyred between 1745 and 1862 -- canonized by John Paul II in 1988. Vietnamese Christianity, planted by Jesuit missionaries in the seventeenth century, has produced one of the most extensive martyrologies in modern Church history. The faith in Vietnam survived centuries of persecution.
saintAndrewDungLacAndCompanionsMartyrs.prayer: O God, who sustained Andrew and his companions in their witness: may the seed of their martyrdom continue to bear fruit in the Church in Vietnam.

saintCatherineOfAlexandriaVirginAndMarty.name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
saintCatherineOfAlexandriaVirginAndMarty.bio: Catherine was a young woman of Alexandria, traditionally of noble or royal birth, martyred under the Emperor Maxentius around 305 AD. She is said to have debated fifty philosophers sent to argue her out of the faith and converted them all; they were subsequently killed. She is one of the fourteen Holy Helpers, among the most widely venerated saints of the Middle Ages, the patron of philosophers, scholars, wheelwrights, and young women. Joan of Arc heard her voice.
saintCatherineOfAlexandriaVirginAndMarty.prayer: O God, who gave Catherine wisdom to confound the wise of this world: grant that we may hold the faith with her confidence and her joy.

saintAndrewTheApostle.name: St. Andrew
saintAndrewTheApostle.bio: Andrew was the first called of the Twelve -- "the Protoclete" in Eastern Christianity. He was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee, a disciple of John the Baptist before following Jesus, and the brother of Simon Peter. It was Andrew who brought Peter to Jesus. According to tradition, he was crucified on an X-shaped cross at Patras in Greece. He is the patron of Scotland, Russia, Greece, and Romania -- as many nations as there are traditions about where he preached.
saintAndrewTheApostle.prayer: O God, who willed that Andrew should be the first to recognize and follow your Son: grant that we may follow him without delay, as Andrew followed his Lord.

saintFrancisXavierPriest.name: St. Francis Xavier
saintFrancisXavierPriest.bio: Francis was a Navarrese nobleman, a student of philosophy in Paris, a housemate of Ignatius of Loyola, and one of the founding members of the Society of Jesus. He spent eleven years (1541–1552) in India, the Malay Archipelago, and Japan -- the first sustained Catholic missionary presence in Asia. He baptized tens of thousands. He died on the island of Sancian, off the coast of China, unable to get permission to enter the country he had come to evangelize. He is the patron saint of missionaries and of the Propagation of the Faith.
saintFrancisXavierPriest.prayer: O God, who inflamed the heart of Francis with apostolic love: grant through his intercession that your Church may reach every nation with the fire of that love.

saintJohnDamascenePriestAndDoctor.name: St. John Damascene
saintJohnDamascenePriestAndDoctor.bio: John of Damascus was a Christian official in the court of the Umayyad Caliph, living under Islamic rule in Damascus, who became a monk at the monastery of Mar Saba in Palestine. He wrote the Fount of Knowledge -- the first systematic summary of Christian theology -- and led the theological defense of the veneration of images during the Iconoclast controversy. His arguments prevailed at the Second Council of Nicaea in 787. He is the last of the Greek Fathers and a Doctor of the Church.
saintJohnDamascenePriestAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who filled John of Damascus with heavenly love and gave him the gifts of wisdom and speech: through his intercession, grant us the grace to hold fast to the holy traditions of your Church.

saintNicholasBishop.name: St. Nicholas
saintNicholasBishop.bio: Nicholas was bishop of Myra in Lycia (modern Turkey) in the fourth century. His biography is almost entirely legendary, but the legends are consistent: he saved three poor girls from prostitution by throwing bags of gold through their window at night; he saved three falsely condemned soldiers by appearing to the Emperor Constantine in a dream; he saved sailors in a storm; he raised three children murdered by a butcher. He is the patron of children, sailors, merchants, the falsely accused, and giving without recognition.
saintNicholasBishop.prayer: O God, who made Nicholas renowned for his generosity to those in need: grant us through his intercession a spirit of giving that seeks no credit.

saintAmbroseBishopAndDoctor.name: St. Ambrose
saintAmbroseBishopAndDoctor.bio: Ambrose was a Roman governor who was elected bishop of Milan by popular acclamation -- he was not yet baptized. He was baptized, ordained, and consecrated bishop in rapid succession in 374. He became the most significant bishop in the West of his generation: he refused to surrender a basilica to the Arian Empress Justina, he compelled the Emperor Theodosius to do public penance for a massacre in Thessaloniki, he baptized Augustine. His hymns are still sung. He established the tradition of episcopal independence from imperial authority.
saintAmbroseBishopAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who raised up Ambrose as a pillar of your Church: grant through his intercession that the Church may always have shepherds who fear you more than kings.

immaculateConception.name: The Immaculate Conception
immaculateConception.bio: The Immaculate Conception -- that Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her existence -- was defined as dogma by Pius IX in 1854. The theology requires care: it is not that she needed no redemption, but that she was redeemed preemptively, by the merits of her Son applied to her in advance. Four years after the definition, she appeared at Lourdes and identified herself as "the Immaculate Conception." The patronal feast of the United States.
immaculateConception.prayer: O God, who by the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin prepared a worthy dwelling for your Son: grant, we pray, that, as you preserved her from every stain by virtue of the death of your Son, which you foresaw, so, through her intercession, we, too, may be cleansed and admitted to your presence.

saintJuanDiegoCuauhtlatoatzin.name: St. Juan Diego
saintJuanDiegoCuauhtlatoatzin.bio: Juan Diego was an Aztec convert who, on December 9 and 12, 1531, ten years after the Spanish conquest of Mexico, saw apparitions of the Virgin Mary on the hill of Tepeyac outside Mexico City. She left her image on his tilma -- the rough cloak he wore. The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe, venerated in the Basilica of Guadalupe in Mexico City, is the most visited Marian shrine in the world. Nine million people visit annually. Juan Diego is the first indigenous American to be canonized.
saintJuanDiegoCuauhtlatoatzin.prayer: O God, who through Our Lady of Guadalupe revealed your tender love for the peoples of America: grant through Juan Diego's intercession that the Gospel may take root in every culture.

saintDamasusIPope.name: St. Damasus I
saintDamasusIPope.bio: Damasus was pope from 366 to 384, one of the most significant occupants of the Roman see. He commissioned Jerome to revise the Latin biblical translations -- the beginning of the Vulgate. He restored and adorned the Roman catacombs, composing verse inscriptions for the tombs of the martyrs that shaped the Church's memory of her early history. He insisted on the primacy of the Roman see. He held the Council of Rome in 382, which established the biblical canon as the Church has received it.
saintDamasusIPope.prayer: O God, who guided Damasus to restore the memory of the martyrs and to commission the translation of your word: grant that we may receive that word with the reverence he gave it.

ourLadyOfGuadalupe.name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
ourLadyOfGuadalupe.bio: On December 12, 1531, the Virgin Mary appeared for the fourth time to Juan Diego on Tepeyac and left her image on his tilma. The image -- an indigenous woman in the iconographic style of an Aztec goddess but with Christian symbols -- spoke directly to the newly conquered people of Mexico in their own visual language. Within ten years of the apparition, nine million Mexicans had converted to Christianity. The image is scientifically inexplicable in its details, has never faded in five centuries, and shows a human figure reflected in the eyes of Mary.
ourLadyOfGuadalupe.prayer: Our Lady of Guadalupe, mystical rose, intercede for the Church, protect the Holy Father, help all those who invoke you in their necessities.

saintLucyOfSyracuseVirginAndMartyr.name: St. Lucy
saintLucyOfSyracuseVirginAndMartyr.bio: Lucy was a Sicilian woman martyred under Diocletian around 304 AD. Her name means light. She is one of the few women mentioned by name in the Roman Canon. According to tradition, she had consecrated her virginity to God and was denounced to the governor by a rejected suitor. She was condemned to a brothel; the soldiers could not move her. She was blinded, or she blinded herself, or she was blinded by her jailers -- the traditions vary. She is the patron of the blind, of writers, and of glaziers.
saintLucyOfSyracuseVirginAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who gave Lucy the grace to keep the light of faith inviolate through martyrdom: through her intercession, grant us light in our darkness.

saintJohnOfTheCrossPriestAndDoctor.name: St. John of the Cross
saintJohnOfTheCrossPriestAndDoctor.bio: Juan de Yepes was a Castilian Carmelite friar who, with Teresa of Ávila, reformed the Carmelite Order and suffered imprisonment by his own brothers for it. His eight months of solitary confinement in a cell six feet by ten feet in Toledo, where he was beaten regularly and nearly starved, produced the first draft of the Spiritual Canticle -- one of the great poems in the Spanish language. His Dark Night of the Soul and The Ascent of Mount Carmel constitute the most systematic mystical theology in the Christian tradition. He is a Doctor of the Church.
saintJohnOfTheCrossPriestAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who endowed John of the Cross with a spirit of self-denial and love of the cross: grant that, imitating him constantly, we may come to contemplate eternally your glory.

saintPeterCanisiusPriestAndDoctor.name: St. Peter Canisius
saintPeterCanisiusPriestAndDoctor.bio: Peter Canisius was a Dutch Jesuit who became the principal figure of the Counter-Reformation in German-speaking lands. He founded the first Jesuit college in Germany, taught, preached, and wrote three catechisms -- one for children, one for educated adults, one for scholars -- that were printed in two hundred editions in his lifetime. He preached more than twenty thousand sermons. He is a Doctor of the Church. Without his work, it is difficult to imagine the survival of Catholicism in central Europe.
saintPeterCanisiusPriestAndDoctor.prayer: O God, who strengthened Peter Canisius in his service of your Church: grant through his intercession the same perseverance in teaching and defending the faith.

saintJohnOfKantyPriest.name: St. John of Kanty
saintJohnOfKantyPriest.bio: John was a Polish professor of theology at the University of Kraków, director of the collegiate church of Saint Anne, and a man of extreme personal austerity and charity. He slept on bare boards. He gave away his clothing to beggars. He made four pilgrimages to Rome on foot and one to Jerusalem. He carried a bag of food for the poor in his belt. He was removed from his professorship once and sent to pastor a parish -- he returned to teaching when the authorities recognized their mistake. He died in 1473 at eighty-three.
saintJohnOfKantyPriest.prayer: O God, who gave John of Kanty the grace to combine learning and poverty: grant that those who seek wisdom may always seek it in the service of the poor.

saintStephenTheFirstMartyr.name: St. Stephen
saintStephenTheFirstMartyr.bio: Stephen was one of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles, "full of faith and of the Holy Spirit." He was seized, tried before the Sanhedrin, and stoned to death outside Jerusalem -- the first martyr of the Christian Church. At his stoning, the witnesses laid their cloaks at the feet of a young man named Saul. As he was dying, Stephen prayed: "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge." Luke notes that Saul consented to his death. The connection between the proto-martyr and the proto-apostle is one of the most significant details in Acts.
saintStephenTheFirstMartyr.prayer: O God, who opened the gates of heaven to your first martyr Stephen: grant us the same love for our enemies and the same vision of your glory.

saintJohnTheApostleAndEvangelist.name: St. John the Apostle
saintJohnTheApostleAndEvangelist.bio: John was the son of Zebedee, brother of James, the Beloved Disciple -- the one who reclined next to Jesus at the Last Supper, who stood at the foot of the cross, who received Mary into his household, who ran to the tomb and believed. He is the author -- in some sense -- of the Fourth Gospel, three letters, and the Book of Revelation. He is the only one of the Twelve who was not martyred, dying peacefully in old age at Ephesus. He was the last surviving eyewitness of the Resurrection.
saintJohnTheApostleAndEvangelist.prayer: O God, who revealed the mysteries of your word to John the Apostle: grant that we may understand what he proclaimed and come to share in the eternal life he described.

holyInnocentsMartyrs.name: The Holy Innocents
holyInnocentsMartyrs.bio: Herod, learning from the Magi that a king had been born in Bethlehem, ordered the killing of all male children under two in the district. The Holy Innocents are the first martyrs of the Christian era -- those who died for Christ without knowing him, without choosing him, without any act of their own. Augustine calls them "flowers before the fruit," cut down by the frost before they could bloom. The massacre of innocents has never stopped, which is why this feast has never stopped being read.
holyInnocentsMartyrs.prayer: O God, whom the Innocents confessed and proclaimed on this day not by speaking but by dying: grant that our lives may bear witness to the faith our lips confess.

saintThomasBecketBishopAndMartyr.name: St. Thomas Becket
saintThomasBecketBishopAndMartyr.bio: Thomas Becket was Henry II's friend, his chancellor, and then -- after Henry had him made Archbishop of Canterbury -- his adversary. The issue was whether the Church or the Crown had ultimate jurisdiction over clergy. Thomas held the Church. Henry held the Crown. Thomas was murdered at his altar in Canterbury Cathedral on December 29, 1170, by four knights who thought they were doing the king's will. Henry did public penance at the tomb. Thomas was canonized three years after his death.
saintThomasBecketBishopAndMartyr.prayer: O God, who gave Thomas Becket the grace to give his life in defense of your Church's liberty: grant that all who serve your Church may do so without counting the cost.

saintSylvesterIPope.name: St. Sylvester I
saintSylvesterIPope.bio: Sylvester was pope from 314 to 335 -- the entire reign of Constantine I. Under him the Church emerged from persecution into imperial favor: the Council of Nicaea (325), the building of the great Roman basilicas, the Christianization of the empire. He did not attend Nicaea personally, sending legates. The Donation of Constantine -- the forged document claiming Constantine gave Sylvester and his successors temporal authority over the Western Empire -- was written in his name. He presided, quietly, over the most dramatic transformation of Christian history.
saintSylvesterIPope.prayer: O God, who guided Sylvester to shepherd your Church in the sudden transition from persecution to freedom: grant wisdom to your Church in every new season of its history.
